items.title: Boké – Éducation : la Fondation Wazni lance, avec l’appui de l’Ambassade de France en Guinée et en Sierra Leone, un programme pilote de renforcement des compétences des enseignants
items.description: COMMUNIQUÉ DE PRESSE Boké, République de Guinée, le 22 octobre 2026 – La Fondation Wazni a lancé, le 30 septembre 2026 au CECOJE de Boké, le volet linguistique de son programme pilote de renforcement des compétences des enseignants. Le dispositif associe une préparation aux certifications DELF et DALF à un accompagnement pédagogique dans trois écoles pilotes de la préfecture. Mis en œuvre avec l’Institut français de Guinée pour le volet linguistique et le GREF – Groupement des Éducateurs sans Frontières pour le volet pédagogique, le programme bénéficie de l’appui de l’Ambassade de France en Guinée et en Sierra Leone, en coordination avec les autorités éducatives locales. Renforcer les compétences linguistiques et pédagogiques Le programme vise à répondre aux besoins identifiés au sein du corps éducatif en renforçant à la fois la maîtrise du français et les pratiques pédagogiques. Le lancement a réuni des représentants des établissements de Donghol, Baralandé, Hadja M’Mah et Khougnèwadé 2, ainsi que de l’ENI, des CPMF, de la DPE et des PEN. Le parcours linguistique prépare les participants aux certifications DELF et DALF, selon leur niveau, 47 participants étaient inscrits au lancement. Le volet pédagogique concerne 30 enseignants référents issus des écoles pilotes de Donghol, Baralandé et Hadja M’Mah. Prévu sur trois ans, il repose sur un accompagnement régulier et le partage progressif des acquis avec les autres enseignants, avec l’ambition de toucher à terme environ 120 enseignants. La première mission des trois formateurs du GREF, qui a officiellement débuté, porte sur la pédagogie générale ainsi que sur l’enseignement du français et des mathématiques, à travers des observations en classe, des visites-conseils et des ateliers collectifs. Les participants auront également accès aux ressources pédagogiques numériques du réseau culturel français, notamment IFprofs, IFclasse et Culturethèque. Un partenariat fondé sur des expertises complémentaires La mise en œuvre du programme s’appuie sur une convention de partenariat conclue en juillet 2026 entre la Fondation Wazni et l’Ambassade de France en Guinée et en Sierra Leone, ainsi que sur une convention-cadre de trois ans entre la Fondation Wazni et le GREF. La Fondation Wazni assure le financement, la coordination et le suivi du programme. Ses partenaires mobilisent leurs expertises respectives, le GREF pour l’accompagnement pédagogique et l’Institut français de Guinée pour le volet linguistique et l’accès aux ressources pédagogiques du réseau culturel français. Céline Wazni, représentante de la Fondation Wazni, déclare : « Investir dans l’éducation, c’est aussi investir dans celles et ceux qui la font vivre au quotidien. Après avoir œuvré sur les infrastructures et les conditions d’apprentissage, nous plaçons désormais les compétences au cœur de notre action. » Un engagement qui évolue avec les besoins du système éducatif Depuis 2020, la Fondation Wazni accompagne le développement de l’éducation dans la région de Boké. Dans le cadre de son programme éducatif, elle a contribué à la construction, la rénovation et l’équipement de 16 établissements scolaires, notamment à travers l’amélioration des salles de classe, bibliothèques, équipements scolaires, de l’accès à l’eau, de l’assainissement, de l’électrification et des espaces informatiques. Avec ce programme, la Fondation Wazni élargit son action au développement des compétences des professionnels de l’éducation, en complément de ses interventions en faveur des infrastructures et des conditions d’apprentissage.

items.title: Makurdi in darkness as electricity workers withdraw services over alleged attack
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State capital, Makurdi, has been thrown into darkness following the withdrawal of services by members of the National Union of Electricity Employees, NUEE, in the Jos Electricity Distribution Plc, JED, chapter, over an alleged attack on some of its members by suspected armed men. The union alleged that the attackers invaded the Makurdi District office of JED, seized the Benue State Operating Officer, Mr. Samson Abah, and an unspecified number of other workers before taking them to the River Benue Bridge, where they were reportedly assaulted. According to the union, the attackers also seized the workers’ mobile phones and other personal belongings, demanded money for their release and allegedly forced them to reconnect electricity supply to the Benue State Government House. The Acting National Secretary of NUEE, Dominic Igwebike, who disclosed this in a statement, said the incident followed the disconnection of electricity supply to Government House over an alleged discovery of meter bypass by government officials. The union’s position came amid an escalating disagreement over electricity supply to the state government’s seat of power, with the Benue State Government dismissing the allegations and accusing JED of making unsubstantiated claims against it. Igwebike said the union could no longer guarantee the safety of its members if they continued to work under the prevailing circumstances, insisting that the withdrawal of services was necessary to protect their lives and property. He said, “Our members cannot continue to work under their brutalised, intimidation and threats to life until we are assured of the safety of our lives and properties.” Confirming the shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, a JED staff member, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak on the matter, said the workers withdrew their services following the alleged attack on their colleagues. “Our office was attacked and our union asked us to withdraw our services, so we have shut down power supply to Makurdi. We have left the office after shutting down, and Makurdi will not have power supply until the matter is resolved with our union,” the staff member said. However, the Benue State Government has strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as baseless, defamatory and an attempt to tarnish its image. In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information, Chief Solomon Iorpev, the government said it would not accept allegations linking it to violence, abduction or illegal electricity connections without credible evidence. The statement read, “The Government of Benue State strongly rejects the baseless and defamatory allegations contained in the press statement issued by Jos Electricity Distribution Plc (JED Plc) on October 22, 2026. The claims that the State Government sanctioned acts of violence, abduction, or illegal electricity connections are reckless, unfounded, and unacceptable.” Addressing the allegations surrounding the reported attack on JED workers, the government questioned the evidence linking it to the incident, arguing that the distribution company had not provided verifiable details to substantiate its claims. According to the statement: “JED Plc’s own use of the word ‘allegedly’ confirms that it has no evidence linking the Government to the incident of October 21, 2026. No names, identities, or credible references were provided. The Government categorically rejects this insinuation.” On the dispute over electricity supply to Government House, the state government said issues concerning transformer energisation and alleged metering irregularities should be handled through the appropriate regulatory and judicial channels. It stated, “Issues of transformer energization and metering irregularities are regulatory matters. They must be addressed before the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and, where necessary, the courts, not through inflammatory press releases. “Assertions of abduction, assault, and injuries remain unsubstantiated. The Government does not condone violence and demands that impartial, evidence-based, and transparent investigations be carried out by security operatives,” the statement added. Expressing displeasure over JED’s handling of the controversy, the government described the company’s public reaction as premature, arguing that it should have allowed security agencies to establish the facts before making allegations in the media. “The reckless outburst by the JED without conclusive investigations is suspicious and amounts to sponsorship by enemies of state to tarnish the image of the government,” the statement alleged. The government also faulted JED’s reference to an earlier incident on September 3, 2026, describing the company’s account as misleading. It challenged the distribution company to produce documentary evidence of its alleged previous communications with the state government over the dispute. “The company has failed to produce records of its alleged ‘several communications’ with the Government. The State challenges JED Plc to publish such correspondence if it exists,” the statement said. Insisting that electricity distribution companies must comply with the same regulatory requirements and safety standards applicable to their customers, the government said JED must also be held accountable for its operations. The statement added: “JED Plc itself acknowledges that interventions must comply with regulatory requirements and safety standards. The Government insists that this standard binds JED Plc as firmly as it binds any customer, including public institutions.” The state government further warned JED against what it described as attempts to politicise its operations and damage the integrity of the state. “The Benue State Government will not tolerate attempts by any business entity to politicize its operations or malign the integrity of the State. JED Plc is hereby strongly warned to desist from making baseless accusations in the media,” it said. Consequently, the government demanded the immediate withdrawal of what it described as the insinuation that it sanctioned violence, a retraction of the allegation that it engaged in meter bypassing or illegal electricity connections, and a formal apology to the government and the people of Benue State. It warned that it would consider legal action if JED persisted in disseminating what it described as false information. “The Government remains committed to the rule of law, the protection of lives and property, and constructive engagement with stakeholders in the electricity sector. However, it will not hesitate to pursue legal remedies should JED Plc persist in disseminating falsehoods,” the statement said. The government added that the people of Benue State deserved reliable electricity supply, respectful treatment and accountability rather than what it termed reckless allegations. As of the time of filing this report, the dispute had resulted in a shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, with the workers insisting that they would not resume operations until the matter was resolved with their union. The post Makurdi in darkness as electricity workers withdraw services over alleged attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: S’East assemblies back state police, warn against political abuse
items.description: By Steve Oko, Vin Ujumadu, Chinedu Adonu & Jeff Agbodo The various Houses of Assembly in the South-East have backed the Bill for State Police. While Anambra , Enugu, Imo and Abia have passed the Bill, Ebonyi House of Assembly is at the verge of passing it into law. The executive bill, which originated from the Presidency, was passed through the first, second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday. The proposed framework allows states to establish their own police services, subject to constitutional provisions and national policing standards prescribed by the National Assembly. Presiding over the plenary, Speaker, Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Somtochukwu Udeze, directed the Clerk to transmit the resolution to the National Assembly. The Majority Leader, Ikenna Ofodeme, said state police would strengthen grassroots security, facilitate quicker responses to threats, create jobs and reduce the military’s involvement in internal security operations. He also proposed integrating local vigilantes into the state policing system after appropriate training. Throwing their weight behind the Bill, the Enugu State House of Assembly, said decentralising the country’s policing architecture would improve security and strengthen the protection of lives and property. The lawmakers expressed their positions on Tuesday, November 20 during plenary while considering a proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Service and related matters. Supporting the proposal, the member representing Ezeagu Constituency, Hon. Chima Obieze, said the establishment of state police would make policing more effective by bringing security operations closer to the people. According to him: “The establishment of State Police will decentralise the policing architecture of the country and make it more effective in the protection of lives and property across the state.” Similarly, the member representing Nkanu East Constituency, Hon. Okey Mbah, said state police could help tackle recurring security challenges, including violence and attacks attributed to herders in different parts of the state. Mbah maintained that a decentralised policing system would enable authorities to respond more effectively to security threats within their respective communities. He said the establishment of state police would help “curtail incessant violence and herdsmen attacks in different parts of the state.” However, the member representing Igbo-Eze South Constituency, Hon. Harrison Ogara, cautioned that the proposed state police system could be abused by political officeholders if adequate safeguards were not established. Ogara expressed concern that state police formations might be used to intimidate political opponents, stressing that effective oversight and accountability mechanisms were necessary to protect the institution from political interference. He said: “State Police formations could be used to intimidate political opponents if adequate safeguards are not put in place.” The lawmaker also called for professional standards, transparent accountability structures and sustainable funding arrangements to ensure that state police personnel discharge their duties without undue political influence. According to him, effective oversight would be essential to ensuring that the proposed security structure serves the public interest rather than the interests of those in power. The Speaker of the House, Chief Uche Ugwu, said the proposed changes to the naming of Nigeria’s policing institutions could also influence institutional orientation and the attitudes of personnel. The proposal includes changing the name of the Nigeria Police Force to the Federal Police Service, alongside the establishment of the State Police Service. Ugwu said the changes could contribute to a shift in institutional orientation and personnel attitudes, potentially improving the delivery of policing services. The proposed constitutional amendment comes amid growing calls for the decentralisation of Nigeria’s security architecture to enable states to respond more effectively to local security challenges. Proponents argue that state police would improve intelligence gathering and response times, while critics have raised concerns about possible political abuse, inadequate funding and the need for strong accountability mechanisms. Ebonyi to pass bill soon — Speaker The Speaker of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Moses Ije Odunwa, has said the Assembly will soon pass the State Police Bill. Odunwa disclosed that lawmakers had commenced deliberations on the bill and were close to completing the process, subject to necessary scrutiny. He said the proposed legislation was aimed at strengthening the protection of lives and property in Ebonyi State and Nigeria at large. The Speaker recalled that Ebonyi State had supported the establishment of state police during the National Assembly’s constitutional review engagement, where the state government and Assembly made submissions in favour of decentralised policing. “We have started deliberating on the bill, and we are very close to its passage,” Odunwa said. Similarly, the Deputy Speaker, Abia State House of Assembly, Austin Nmeregini, told Vanguard on Thursday afternoon that the Abia lawmakers were at the verge of passing the Bill. He disclosed that the Bill had already received the support of the lawmakers during their Executive session, hinting that they were proceeding into plenary where it will ultimately be passed into law. He said that the passage of the Bill into law would help address peculiar security challenges of every state as every state better understands its own terrain more than strangers. Later in the day, the Abia State House of Assembly voted in favour of the State Police Bill. The Acting Clerk Abia State House of Assembly, Mr Promise confirmed this in an interview with Vanguard. Speaking later with Vanguard, Deputy Speaker Nmeregini, said that the State Police Bill was passed by “unanimous vote.” The post S’East assemblies back state police, warn against political abuse appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: America Needs Its Indian Immigrants
items.description: Ask many successful Indian CEOs, entrepreneurs, or scientists how they rose to prominence in America, and they will tell you that, grit and talent aside, the key factor was the country itself: an economy and a culture that rewarded merit and drew ambitious, talented people from around the world. Indian Americans are among the most affluent and best-educated groups in the country. What distinguishes them from other immigrant groups is that they have risen to the top in one generation. Median household income for Indian Americans is $151,200, compared with $92,530 for white Americans . About three-quarters of Indian adults 25 and older in the U.S. hold a bachelor’s degree, against a national average of 38 percent. Nearly half have graduate degrees, and the poverty rate, 6 percent, is among the lowest of any ethnic group. Indian Americans tend to be employed and law-abiding. For a community more accustomed to being called the “model minority” or “ tech’s new titans ,” a recent rise in anti-Indian rhetoric —now commonplace on sites and apps such as X, YouTube, and Reddit—has been a shock. According to Stop AAPI Hate , nearly half of South Asian adults living in America reported having been targeted in a “race-based hate act” in 2025 alone. From 2023 to 2025, the use of anti–South Asian slurs online surged by 109 percent. The Trump administration has also attacked immigrants coming from India with efforts to severely restrict the H-1B visa program, a legal pathway to American jobs; 70 percent of H-1B recipients are Indian. Despite two different judges blocking President Trump’s $100,000 fee for the visa, the administration claims that applications are down 92 percent at the largest IT-staffing and -outsourcing firms—a decline that it views as a massive success. Indian immigrants have helped make this country great. America has long needed Indian immigrants, and it still does. But people who don’t understand the great contributions of Indian Americans would rather close the door, and are hostile to those who are already here. By 1960, Europeans made up 75 percent of all immigrants in the U.S. By 2010, the balance had reversed, and Europeans were just 12 percent of all immigrants. According to U.S. Census Bureau data, in 1990 fewer than a million Indians were living in the U.S. A decade later, their numbers doubled because of a hiring spree for engineers to help avert a potential Y2K crisis. Today, some 5.2 million Indians reside in America, more than 60 percent of whom were born in India. Although they represent just 1.5 percent of the population, their sudden success has made them very visible—and that visibility has made them targets. [ Jonathan Chait: The mainstreaming of anti-Indian bigotry ] Indian-born executives are running several of the biggest technology companies, such as Google, Microsoft, IBM, and Adobe. They have been at the center of some people’s anger over AI and layoffs throughout the tech industry. In politics, the rise of Ro Khanna, Vivek Ramaswamy, Kamala Harris, and Zohran Mamdani has also caused online and real-life hate toward those with Indian heritage. For Americans uneasy about how the country is changing, seeing Indians in charge can feel more like a threat than a hopeful sign about the viability of the American dream. Immigration politics have always been tangled up with discrimination. In the 1850s, the United States brought in cheap Chinese laborers to work its mines, farms, and railroads. When the economy shrank during the 1870s, the cry of “they’re taking our jobs”—familiar today—led to the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882, which restricted Chinese immigration for the next 60 years. Japanese and, later, Korean workers met the same antagonism, and the Immigration Act of 1917, also known as the Asiatic Barred Zone Act, effectively shut out immigrants from most of Asia. The country went through a long period of xenophobia that targeted not only nonwhite immigrants but also “undesirable” white immigrants, such as Italians and Eastern European Jews. In 1910, the foreign-born population was 14.7 percent; by 1960, it had fallen to 5.4 percent. In 1965, the Immigration and Nationality Act eased the old restrictions, in large part because the country was short of skilled labor, particularly in the STEM fields. Two developments drove the change. The first was Sputnik. In 1957, the Soviet Union launched the first satellite into space. The U.S. military, fearful it was losing the Cold War, began investing heavily in science, sending large sums to top research universities. By the ’60s, the race had accelerated, but engineers were in short supply, so the country began recruiting overseas. Starting in 1950, India, in collaboration with foreign partners, had begun building world-class engineering schools called the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). Well-trained, English-speaking engineers began graduating just as the U.S. was desperate for them. India had hoped that these engineers would help drive its own development, but it offered too few jobs, and the U.S. had found an ideal recruiting ground. Even today, the IITs remain fiercely selective, accepting less than 1 percent of roughly 1 million applicants per year. Sundar Pichai, the CEO of Google; Vinod Khosla, a venture capitalist and co-founder of Sun Microsystems; and Arvind Krishna, the CEO of IBM, are all IIT graduates. The first wave of Indian engineers was recruited after 1965. A second big wave came in the late ’90s, during Y2K preparations. The second development was a need for doctors. In July 1965, President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Medicare and Medicaid Act, and almost overnight, 20 million Americans became eligible for health care. Hospitals lacked the staff to cope. The Vietnam War was escalating, medical personnel were being sent to the front, and disabled veterans were returning home needing long-term care. Hospitals looked overseas, and India again supplied trained professionals to a strained system. Indian doctors were on the front lines of the AIDS epidemic in the ’80s and the coronavirus pandemic in the early 2020s. [ Meenakshi Ahamed: America has never really understood India ] The U.S. has benefited from the skills that Indians bring without having had to invest much in their education. Many have earned advanced degrees in America, but the bulk of their training happened in India. A more honest way to see it is that India, along with other poorer countries, has been subsidizing the United States. Presidents like to define their eras with a slogan that conveys the legacy they hope to leave. John F. Kennedy called his the “New Frontier.” He was determined to win the Cold War and stop the spread of communism, and pushed the country toward space exploration while investing in science and technology. Johnson’s was the “Great Society.” His goal was to care for the elderly and the poor. Having known poverty firsthand, he wanted to extend health care to the vulnerable, and he signed both the Medicare and the Civil Rights Acts. Both of these presidents’ visions leaned on importing talent from abroad. Trump’s slogan is “Make America Great Again.” Yet one of his lasting legacies may be that he turned his back on the very talent that helped make America great in the first place.

items.title: Tinubu backs local engineers to unlock gas pipeline capacity
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his commitment to unlocking Nigeria’s gas resources to power industries, improve electricity supply, create jobs and boost export earnings, backing indigenous engineering firms to play a greater role in major energy projects. The President spoke against the backdrop of Lee Engineering Group’s construction of two compressor stations designed to enable the Escravos–Lagos Pipeline System (ELPS) to operate at its full capacity of 2.3 billion standard cubic feet of gas per day. Tinubu made the remarks while receiving the Founder and Chairman of Lee Engineering Group, Chief Dr Leemon Ikpea, at the State House, Abuja. He reaffirmed his administration’s Nigeria First policy and urged international oil companies operating in the country to provide more opportunities for competent Nigerian engineering and manufacturing firms to participate in major energy projects. Lee Engineering is handling the engineering, procurement and construction of two midline compressor stations in Edo State. Although the ELPS II expansion increased the pipeline’s designed capacity from 1.1 billion to 2.3 billion standard cubic feet of gas per day, the compressor stations are required to raise operating pressure and enable the system to deliver at its full capacity. The project is expected to strengthen gas transportation to power plants and industries along the pipeline corridor, support increased supplies to neighbouring West African countries through the West African Gas Pipeline, and create opportunities for additional export earnings. Tinubu said the Nigeria First policy must translate into more contracts for capable indigenous firms, greater use of locally manufactured equipment and the creation of skilled jobs for Nigerians. He encouraged international oil companies to build stronger partnerships with Nigerian engineering companies that had demonstrated the capacity to deliver complex projects. The President also highlighted his administration’s 2024 executive orders and presidential directives on local content compliance, contracting costs and approval timelines, describing them as measures to attract investment, reduce delays and expand opportunities for Nigerian businesses. Ikpea commended the President’s Nigeria First policy, disclosing that Lee Engineering’s fabrication yard in Warri, Delta State, was manufacturing some components for the compressor stations. He said the facility housed some of the industry’s most advanced fabrication equipment. Ikpea added that Nigerian companies had invested significantly in modern equipment, technology and skilled personnel, enabling them to undertake complex engineering, procurement and construction projects previously handled by foreign contractors. He said greater participation by indigenous firms would help retain more jobs, expertise and economic value within Nigeria. items.title: À Linguère, les écailleuses de poisson à la force des mains
items.description: Au marché central de Linguère, des femmes et de jeunes hommes passent leurs journées à écailler des poissons, les mains dans l’eau et le dos courbé. Rémunérée à la tâche, cette activité leur permet de subvenir aux besoins de leurs familles. Mais entre revenus irréguliers, coupures fréquentes et absence de protection, ces travailleurs réclament de meilleures conditions. LINGUÈRE – Dès les premières heures du matin, le marché central de Linguère s’éveille. Sous les tôles ondulées, les vendeurs installent leurs étals tandis que les appels des commerçants se mêlent aux marchandages des clients. Dans l’air se croisent les odeurs d’épices, de fumée de bois et de poisson frais. Dans la partie réservée aux produits halieutiques, les bassines débordent de sardinelles, de capitaines, de daurades, de tilapias et d’autres espèces. Les vendeuses interpellent les passants. Les couteaux frappent les bassines, les voix s’élèvent et les négociations vont bon train. Au milieu de cette agitation, des femmes et de jeunes hommes sont à la tâche. Courbés au-dessus de leurs bassines, ils frottent les poissons, retirent les écailles et les préparent pour les clients. Les gestes sont rapides, précis et répétitifs. Les mains plongées dans l’eau, ils travaillent pendant des heures, malgré l’humidité et les risques de coupure. Pour beaucoup, ce métier est bien plus qu’un service rendu aux vendeuses de poisson : c’est un moyen de faire vivre leur famille. « Nous travaillons debout ou courbés toute la journée, les mains dans l’eau et les écailles. C’est fatigant, mais c’est ce qui nous permet de nourrir nos enfants et de payer leur scolarité », confie Fatou Barry, doyenne du métier et présidente de l’association des femmes écailleuses de Linguère. Selon elle, cette activité répond aussi à une demande des consommateurs, nombreux à préférer acheter du poisson déjà nettoyé. « Nos clients veulent des poissons prêts à cuire. Sans nous, la vente serait plus compliquée », explique-t-elle. Abdou Fall, qui exerce ce métier depuis trois ans, partage ce constat. « Ce n’est pas un travail facile, mais il nous donne une certaine autonomie. Chaque bassine écaillée est une garantie de revenu pour la journée », souligne le jeune homme. Des revenus modestes, mais essentiels Au marché central de Linguère, les écailleuses sont payées à la tâche, généralement selon le nombre de bassines ou de lots de poissons traités. Les gains journaliers oscillent entre 2 000 et 5 000 FCFA, en fonction de la quantité de poisson disponible et du travail accompli. Pour Fama Kobar, qui exerce depuis une vingtaine d’années, chaque journée est une course contre la montre. Souriante et d’un abord facile, elle a su tirer de ce métier des revenus qui lui ont permis de développer d’autres activités. « Chaque bassine écaillée me rapporte environ 500 FCFA. Si je parviens à en faire dix dans la journée, je peux rentrer avec 5 000 FCFA. C’est pénible, mais cet argent nous permet d’acheter du riz et des légumes », raconte-t-elle. Ces gains restent toutefois incertains. Lorsque le poisson se fait rare, les bassines se remplissent moins vite et les revenus diminuent. Certaines journées, les travailleuses doivent se contenter d’environ 2 000 FCFA. Malgré cela, elles continuent de se rendre au marché, faute d’une autre source de revenus régulière. Fatou Ndiaye, qui vient de se lancer dans cette activité, en mesure déjà les exigences. « Au début, je pensais que ce métier serait plus rentable. Mais il demande beaucoup de force, d’assiduité et de patience », reconnaît-elle. Même modestes et irréguliers, ces revenus contribuent aux dépenses quotidiennes des ménages. Ils permettent de participer à l’achat de nourriture et à la prise en charge des enfants, sans pour autant mettre les travailleuses à l’abri de la précarité. Des conditions de travail à améliorer Derrière leur contribution à la vie du marché, les écailleuses et les écailleurs du Djolof font face à des difficultés persistantes. L’absence d’équipements de protection expose leurs mains aux coupures, tandis que l’eau et l’humidité rendent les longues journées encore plus éprouvantes. « Le plus grand défi, c’est l’absence de protection. Nous travaillons les mains dans l’eau toute la journée et les coupures sont fréquentes. Avec des gants et des tabliers, ce serait plus supportable », plaide Rokhaya Ndao, écailleuse au marché central. À ces risques s’ajoute la dépendance à l’approvisionnement en poisson. Lorsque les arrivages diminuent, les revenus suivent la même tendance. Abdou Ndiaye, jeune écailleur, appelle ainsi à un meilleur accompagnement de la profession. « Nos revenus dépendent de l’arrivée du poisson. Quand il y a pénurie, on ne gagne presque rien. Il nous faut davantage de stabilité, peut-être grâce à une organisation qui nous soutienne », estime-t-il. Les travailleurs sollicitent l’appui des pouvoirs publics et des organisations non gouvernementales pour moderniser leur activité et améliorer leurs conditions de travail. Ils soulignent également leur contribution à l’économie locale : selon leur témoignage, la municipalité leur demande de payer une taxe de 100 FCFA par jour. À la tête de l’association des écailleuses et écailleurs du marché central, Fatou Barry indique que la structure compte une cinquantaine de membres. Elle souhaite que ces travailleurs puissent bénéficier d’un soutien de l’État, notamment à travers la Délégation générale à l’entrepreneuriat rapide des femmes et des jeunes (DER/FJ), à l’image d’autres groupements de promotion féminine du département. Au marché central de Linguère, les couteaux continueront de racler les écailles dès les premières heures du jour. Mais derrière ces gestes devenus familiers se trouve une activité essentielle à la vie du marché, qui fait vivre des familles tout en restant confrontée à la précarité. Pour ces travailleurs, la reconnaissance du métier doit désormais s’accompagner de moyens concrets pour exercer dans de meilleures conditions. Abdoulaye Sadio (Correspondant)

items.title: 4 cops including DSP martyred, 2 terrorists killed during exchange of fire in KP's Karak: police
items.description: LAKKI MARWAT: Four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district on Thursday, police said. A statement by the KP police said law enforcers had initiated a search and strike operation in the Charpara area at noon, where terrorists had set up a blockade on Wednesday night. Banda Daud Shah and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) deputy superintendents of police (DSP) led the operation, in which bomb disposal unit (BDU) personnel, a drone team, Rescue 15 personnel and Rapid Response Force personnel also participated, the statement said. “During the operation, the law enforcers raided the hideout of a terrorist commander, Qaiser Iqbal, where an exchange of fire took place,” the police said, adding that two terrorists were killed in the encounter. CTD DSP Imranuddin Khan, Latambar Station House Officer (SHO) Sub-Inspector (SI) Afzal Awan, Constable Kazim and Head Constable Amjad from the BDU were martyred in the exchange of fire. The statement said the operation was ongoing. It added, “The brave martyred personnel of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police have set a shining example of dedication to duty, courage, and a commitment to public safety by sacrificing their lives in the fight against terrorism.” The statement said the sacrifices of the martyred policemen reflected the police force’s “unwavering resolve” to continue making every possible effort to eradicate terrorism and establish lasting peace in the region. Later, the funeral prayers for the martyred police personnel were offered with full official honours. According to the KP police, the funeral was attended by KP Inspector General of Police (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed, CTD Additional IG Jawad Qamar, Kohat Regional Police Officer Shakir Hussain Dawar, Kohat Commissioner Parvez Khan Sabt Khel, CTD Senior Superintendent of Police (Operations) Najamul Hasnain, Karak Deputy Commissioner Hamid Iqbal and Karak District Police Officer Niaz Muhammad, among other high-ranking civil and military and police officers, the families of the martyred personnel, and others. A police contingent presented a final salute to the martyrs, while high-ranking officers paid tribute to them by laying floral wreaths on their coffins. “The attendees honoured the supreme sacrifices offered by the martyrs, prayed for the elevation of their ranks, and sought patience for the bereaved families,” the police statement added. Police officers pay tribute to the martyred police personnel during funeral prayers in KP’s Karak on Oct 22. — photo courtesy KP police KP IGP Hameed paid tributes to the bravery, sense of duty, and professional commitment of the martyrs. He stressed the great courage of the KP police personnel in laying down their lives while confronting terrorists. “The martyrs’ bravery, unwavering dedication to duty, and unparalleled sacrifices for the protection of the public serve as a guiding light for the entire police force,” he added. Earlier, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the incident and expressed sorrow over the martyrdom of four police personnel. “The sacrifices of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police in the fight against terrorism are unforgettable. The blood of our martyrs will not go to waste; our resolve against terrorism will be further strengthened, and the struggle for the establishment of peace will continue,” he said in an X post. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time, including attacks on police personnel. Thursday’s operation comes around 20 days after several terrorist hideouts were destroyed during a joint search and strike operation in Karak. In September, two terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Lakki Marwat, and in August, a police constable was martyred and six officials were injured when an improvised explosive device was used to attack a police patrol van. According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide. Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

items.title: Domestic crude supply to refineries falls 6.3% — NMDPRA
items.description: — Petrol supply drops 20.6% By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Domestic crude oil supply to Nigerian refineries fell by 6.3 per cent to 15.97 million barrels in September 2026 from 17.05 million barrels in August, while petrol supply from domestic refineries also declined amid reduced imports. The September 2026 Midstream and Downstream Report released by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) on Thursday showed that average daily petrol receipts dropped by 23.4 per cent to 38.7 million litres from 50.5 million litres in August. The report attributed the decline to lower domestic supply and reduced imports following the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. Between January and September 2026, Nigerian refineries received a combined 156.51 million barrels of crude oil, comprising 125.85 million barrels of domestic crude and 30.66 million barrels of imported crude. Domestic crude accounted for 80.4 per cent of total refinery intake during the period, while imported crude contributed 19.6 per cent. The report also showed that Dangote Refinery operated at 105.98 per cent utilisation in September, processing approximately 689,000 barrels of crude oil per day against average crude receipts of 618,000 barrels per day. The difference of about 71,000 barrels per day was drawn from the refinery’s inventory, indicating that it processed more crude than it received during the month. On petrol supply, the NMDPRA data showed that domestic refineries supplied an average of 28.5 million litres per day in September, down 20.6 per cent from 35.9 million litres in August. Petrol imports also declined by 30.1 per cent to 10.2 million litres per day from 14.6 million litres. Despite the decline, domestic refineries remained the largest source of petrol supply, accounting for approximately 73.6 per cent of total receipts in September, compared with 26.4 per cent from imports. The September average of 38.7 million litres per day was also below the 13-month average of 49.7 million litres per day recorded between September 2025 and September 2026. Over the 13-month period, domestic refineries supplied an average of 30.4 million litres of petrol per day, representing 61.2 per cent of total supply, while imports contributed 19.3 million litres per day, or 38.8 per cent. The NMDPRA reiterated that September’s decline in petrol receipts reflected a 21 per cent drop in domestic supply from August levels and a 30 per cent reduction in imports amid the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. items.title: NDC members raise security concerns over Kwabre East constituency executive elections
items.description: Some members and sympathisers of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Kwabre East Constituency have raised concerns over alleged security threats ahead of the constituency executive elections scheduled for Saturday, October 25. The members say the prevailing atmosphere raises concerns about whether the polls can be conducted peacefully and credibly. They have questioned the decision by the Constituency Election Committee to hold the election at the Islamic Hall at Aboaso-Zongo, citing what they describe as security risks based on information gathered locally. Addressing a press conference at Mamponteng on Thursday, NDC Ward Secretary for Fawoade-Bampenase, Saeed Abdul Mumin, alleged that intimidation and threats were creating fear among party members ahead of the internal contest. He claimed some supporters of aspirants had received threatening messages and verbal warnings from opponents. “This election is filled with fear and panic because some of us have been receiving threats on our various platforms from the opponent’s camp that they will bring pepper spray to the venue,” he said. “We are worried about this move because this is an internal election, so what would make someone take such a decision?” he asked. Members question choice of venue Mr Mumin also questioned the suitability of the Islamic Hall as the polling venue, arguing that its location near the residence of the incumbent constituency chairman, who is seeking re-election, could raise perceptions of bias. He said the facility was not an open and easily accessible public space and called for a venue that would inspire confidence among all contestants. Mr Mumin further accused the Kwabre East Municipal Chief Executive, Joseph Amankwah, of openly campaigning for some candidates, alleging that his conduct undermined the neutrality expected of him. The allegations have not been independently verified. Petition sent to security authorities The Branch Organiser for Achiase, Charles Owusu, said the concerned members had petitioned Mr Amankwah, who also chairs the Municipal Security Council, as well as the Ashanti Regional Minister and the Ashanti Regional Police Command. According to him, the petitions were intended to alert the authorities to potential security risks ahead of the polls. He said the Constituency Election Committee had nevertheless maintained its decision to use the Aboaso-Zongo venue. Mr Owusu warned that the relevant authorities could face criticism if violence occurred after concerns had been raised in advance. “All we want is a peaceful election. We count on the security agencies and party leadership to monitor the process and ensure that delegates and party members can safely go to the polling centre to cast their votes,” he said. NDC members appeal for intervention Other members who addressed the press conference called on the Ashanti Regional and national executives of the NDC to intervene to prevent possible disturbances. They said the election should be free, fair, transparent and peaceful to preserve unity within the constituency ahead of the 2028 general elections. One member warned that a process perceived as unfair or marred by violence could deepen divisions within the party. The NDC constituency executive elections are scheduled for Saturday, October 25. The concerned members say they want party leaders and security agencies to address their concerns before voting begins.

items.title: Edo govt demolishes building allegedly used for organ harvesting, cultism
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu A house in Uwalor-Oke in Uromi, Esan North East Local Government Area of Edo State has been demolished for allegedly being used for cult activities and organ harvesting. Besides the demolition, the suspected organ harvester Ebhata Eromosele was also arrested by the Edo State Special Security Squad codenamed Operation Flush out Kidnapping and Cultists, in collaboration with Edo State Security Corps, the Nigerian Police Force and other sister security agencies, supervised by the Principal Security Officer (PSO) to the governor. The building was said to have been used for ritual activities where Eromosele was alleged to have harvested the organs of three young women, out of which one of the victims, a pregnant woman, died in the process; one who was hospitalised has been discharged while another is receiving treatment in an undisclosed hospital in Esan Central Senatorial District. Another building located at Idi-Negbon Eguare Ewatto, allegedly used for cult-related activities, was also not spared as it was touched by bulldozers. In a statement by Governor Monday Okpebholo’s Chief Press Secretary, Dr. Patrick Ebiojele, the coordinator of the Special Security Squad, Amiolemen Idemudia said criminals would be wiped out of Edo State. He noted that Ebhata Eromosele engaged in ritual activities before nemesis caught up with him and have been arrested and today his building is demolished in Uromi. He said, “A lifeless body killed and dumped was traced by Edo State Security Corps to this bungalow apartment used by the suspect. “A search of this residence exposed the suspect as security operative saw bloodstained bedspread and other incriminating evidence indicating that Ebhata is into ritual activities and organ harvesting.” Idemudia said the governor has warned that his administration will not tolerate crime of this nature and will make the state unsafe for criminal elements. On the cult issue, Idemudia said there were cult fracas in Ewatto disturbing the peace of the community. He said that one Bright Ejetuwamen was at the forefront of the fight, using his properties at Ewatto for cult-related activities. He said the property has been demolished. “Governor Monday Okpebholo will not spare any hideout or properties used to perpetrate crime as it will be demolished. The cultist has been apprehended. All criminals must leave Edo State,” he said. The Zonal Commander, Edo State Security Corps, SP Johnson Oyameda (rtd), said the success recorded in the arrest of the ritual suspect was as a result of over a month of surveillance. “The body of a lady mutilated and dumped in a drainage was recovered while still alive. Not up to two weeks another body was recovered again and these incidents led to stepping up surveillance around the area and the surveillance paid off. “Ebhata Eromosele murdered a lady and dumped the body but my men on surveillance saw him and trailed him to this apartment which has been demolished today,” he said. Both the suspected ritualists and cultists have been arrested and are in the custody of the Edo State Police Command for further investigation and prosecution. items.title: Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye to meet European trio in Istanbul
items.description: Turkiye will host an R-4 and an R-4+E-3 meeting of foreign ministers in Istanbul on October 23, the Turkish foreign ministry said on Thursday. The R-4 group, which comprises Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran. The E-3 group is a trio of European powers — France, Britain and Germany — that was set up more than 20 years ago to advance diplomatic coordination over Iran’s nuclear programme. The Foreign Office in Islamabad has yet to comment on the planned meetings and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar’s participation. A Turkish diplomatic source told Reuters that the seven countries would meet in the R-4+E-3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran , Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security. The ministers are expected to discuss the Israeli-Palestinian issue, the latest situation in the Strait of Hormuz, developments related to Yemen, efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, and opportunities for closer cooperation between the regional and European countries, the source added. Fidan is expected to emphasise the need for a diplomatic solution to the war between the United States and Iran, the importance of freedom of navigation in the straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, and reiterate Turkiye’s support for Saudi Arabia’s security against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Islamabad, Ankara, and Riyadh, they said. Fidan will also tell counterparts that Turkiye has been working to stop the war in Ukraine from spreading to the Black Sea, pointing to the regional security risks posed by the conflict, the source said.

items.title: Direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives on the horizon as PM stresses connectivity
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday announced that he had issued instructions for direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives. The premier was addressing the Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum, attended by visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, who arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday for a three-day trip at the invitation of PM Shehbaz. The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established in 1966. PM Shehbaz said, “I want to say that connectivity is very important. We don’t have direct flights from Malé to Islamabad or Karachi, so this air link is very important. “I have already given instructions to our ministry of civil aviation to prepare a quick feasibility [study], be it Pakistan International Airlines, or any other airline in Pakistan, to find the ways and means to take the first flight comprising tourists [and the] business community to Malé,” he announced. The premier said he had been informed by President Muizzu that he gave instructions “to his airline to work out a quick plan to start flights from [the] Maldives to Pakistan”. “I have given instructions to our civil aviation department to immediately invite a delegation from [the] Maldives and work out a plan whereby we can start these air flights between the two countries as early as possible,” PM Shehbaz added. Moreover, the premier highlighted the importance of maritime connectivity, noting that unless there is a reliable direct shipping schedule from Karachi or Gwadar to Malé, “we will not be able to meet our targets efficiently and effectively.” He added that once Muizzu returned to his country, a delegation of Pakistani government officials and businessmen would be sent to Malé. He said that the delegation would arrive within the next week or so. Calling Muizzu a “very sincere friend of Pakistan”, the premier hailed his visit as a “turning point in further strengthening our bilateral, brotherly relations” and a “game-changer in terms of promoting our bilateral trade and investment portfolios”. “I would like to convey this message to our great entrepreneurs, traders, investors and businessmen from both [the] Maldives and Pakistan,” he added. “Here is an opportunity we can really convert into … a concrete action plan.” Citing figures provided by Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan, PM Shehbaz said that the trade volume between Islamabad and Malé is approximately $13 million. “My brother, President Dr Muizzu, on my request, readily agreed to make a firm understanding to increase our bilateral trade from $13m to $200m in the next two years, and now it’s all up to us to make use of this opportunity, do our homework and make full preparation to achieve these targets through joint efforts and very close coordination,” the prime minister stated. Taking the podium, President Muizzu echoed PM Shehbaz and urged the establishment of an air corridor between Pakistan and the Maldives. “In this regard, I am pleased to announce that Maldivian, our national airline, aims to establish [a] direct air link between Malé and Karachi soon,” he announced. “This service will make travel easier for the people of our two countries, creating new opportunities for trade and tourism.” He thanked PM Shehbaz for taking the time to attend the forum and said that his presence was “a testament to the close friendship and our shared commitment to strengthening economic cooperation”. “It is such a great pleasure for me to be with you today in Islamabad. And particularly to address a gathering of those who drive enterprise, investment, and economic opportunity in our two countries,” he added. “As we mark 60 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the relationship between the Maldives and Pakistan is rooted in deep fraternal affection, and above all, in the enduring bond of our Islamic faith.” Muizzu noted that while Islamabad and Malé had strong political solidarity and diplomatic trust, their economic relationship had yet to reach its full potential. “We must now define the ambition of our future,” the Maldivian president said. “The time has come to transform the strength of our friendship into a new era of trade, investment, and shared prosperity, which is why yesterday Prime Minister Sharif and I agreed to enhance our bilateral trade to $200m over the next two years.” He added, “Beyond the numbers, this ambitious target is investing in our people. We are not only creating new opportunities for businesses on both sides, but also fostering greater regional prosperity and long-term stability.” Muizzu said Pakistan possessed tremendous potential and that the economies of both nations had “important complementarities”. “For the Maldives, food security is not merely a commercial consideration. As an island nation, resilient supply chains are a matter of national security, and the scale of our market should not be underestimated,” he explained. Noting that Pakistan’s agricultural sector already serves the island nation, Muizzu emphasised the need to move beyond a typical buyer and seller relationship into partnerships in cold chain logistics, temperature-controlled storage, modern food processing and climate-adaptive agricultural technology. “But trade requires connectivity. For an island nation, maritime connectivity is an economic lifeline. We must create more efficient corridors through which that trade can move,” he highlighted. “Therefore, I encourage shipping, port and logistics companies from both countries to explore direct and commercially viable connections between Pakistan and the Maldives.” Stressing the importance of healthcare infrastructure, the Maldivian president highlighted that the country is making significant investments to move from regional tertiary hospitals to modern island-level facilities. “Our demand for reliable, high-quality and certified medical supplies will therefore continue to grow. We welcome Pakistani pharmaceutical manufacturers and healthcare providers,” Muizzu said. Furthermore, he invited Pakistan’s construction companies, developers, manufacturers and engineering firms to partner with the Maldives in housing, land reclamation and connectivity projects, as part of Malé’s endeavours in infrastructure and urban development. “Renewable energy is another area of enormous potential. The Maldives spends hundreds of millions of dollars each year importing diesel. For us, therefore, the transition to clean energy is not only a climate imperative, it is an economic and fiscal necessity,” he added. “My administration has set a target of producing 33 per cent of our national electricity requirement from renewable sources by 2028. That means more than quadrupling more than the amount generated in a five-year period.” Additionally, the Maldivian president highlighted opportunities in both nations, unlocking the power of the global Islamic economy through Sharia-compliant finance, and halal tourism and products. “The Maldives is strengthening its financial landscape and institutional frameworks for Islamic finance,” he said. “Together, our financial institutions, regulators, and businesses can explore Sharia-compliant investment instruments, sukuk , Islamic financial services and halal value chains. And these areas are by no means exhaustive.” Muizzu also highlighted opportunities in tourism and hospitality, IT, education and other sectors and invited Pakistani businesses to “not look at the Maldives merely as a market to sell to, [but] look at the Maldives as a partner to build with”. Later, the Maldivian president expressed his gratitude to PM Shehbaz for his presence at the business forum and for “highlighting the key priorities that will guide our economic partnership into a new chapter”. In a post on X, he said that the forum marked an important first step towards realising the ambition of increasing bilateral trade over the next two years. “I warmly invite Pakistani businesses and investors to explore the wealth of opportunities the Maldives has to offer,” Muizzu said, stating his confidence that the renewed commitment would “forge meaningful partnerships, attract investment, and deliver tangible benefits” to both Pakistan and the Maldives. “Let us build an economic partnership that reflects the strength of our enduring friendship, one that creates opportunities for our peoples, advances shared prosperity, and translates our common aspirations into lasting progress,” he added.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS to reopen to continuing students next week – GES
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) says continuing students of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) are expected to return to school next week, following a temporary closure that began in August. In a press release issued on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and signed by its Head of Public Relations, Daniel Fenyi, the Service said preparations were far advanced for the resumption of academic work. The school was temporarily closed to continuing students on August 5 following disturbances on campus. “Management assures that preparations are far advanced for continuing students to return to school sometime next week,” the statement said. The GES noted that first-year students had reported to the school on September 18, 2026, and were already attending classes. However, the Service did not announce a specific date for the return of continuing students. The closure followed campus disturbances reportedly linked to tensions surrounding sexual abuse allegations against the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. The GES has suspended the headmaster, while the police have forwarded the case docket to the Office of the Attorney-General for study and advice. The allegations have involved as many as 19 students, according to previous reports. They remain subject to investigation and the legal process. The planned reopening would allow continuing students to resume academic work after more than two months away from school. The GES said further updates would be communicated when necessary.

items.title: Many Northern states pass state police bill into law; others dither
items.description: …Benue, Kebbi, Nasarawa, Plateau, Taraba, Zamfara, Yobe pass bill into law …Borno, Katsina, Bauchi, Adamawa, Kano and Jigawa still brainstorming on bill A crucial legislation which was initiated at the National Assembly to empower states to establish their police forces and use for maintaining security, which was sent to the state Houses of Assembly for adoption into state laws, has been given acceleration by many of the 19 northern states. Our correspondents find out that the bill has already been passed into law in Benue, Kebbi, Nasarawa, Plateau, Taraba, Zamfara and Yobe states. However, states such as Borno, Adamawa, Bauchi, Katsina, Kano and Bauchi are still brainstorming on the security legislation. By Soni Daniel, Editor, Northern Region, Umar Yusuf (Yola), Peter Duru (Makurdi), Ndahi Marama (Maiduguri), Femi Bolaji (Jalingo), Haruna Aliyu (Birnin Kebbi), Golok Nanmwa (Jos), Hadiza Yusuf (Kano), Edwin Phillips (Lafia), Idris Salisu (Gusau), Fauziyya Lawal (Katsina), Maryam Usman (Damaturu), Christopher Ameh (Bauchi), Muhammad Inuwa (Dutse), Birnin Kebbi: The bill was received with joy once it got to the floor of the Kebbi State House of Assembly and it was deliberated upon and eventually passed into law that empowers the state to set up its own police. The Kebbi State House of Assembly aligned with the position of the National Assembly and recommended the alteration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and for related matters. This followed the presentation of the report of the House Committee on Home Affairs and Internal Security, led by Muhammad Garba Bena, during Wednesday’s plenary session, presided over by the Speaker of the Assembly, Salihu Maikasuwa Dangoje. After the presentation of the report, the House proceeded to a vote, in which 20 out of the 24 members present at the sitting voted in favour of the establishment of State Police Services, while 4 members were officially absent. Thereafter, the House, led by the Speaker, adopted the position of the National Assembly and recommended that the Bill for the Establishment of State Police Services (Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 Sixth Alteration Bill, 2026) be passed, having secured the required two-thirds majority from the Kebbi State House of Assembly, as stipulated by the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended). The Plateau State House of Assembly has also adopted the position of the NASS and passed the state police bill into law without much delay. The decision was taken during plenary on Tuesday presided over by the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Naanlong Daniel, following the presentation of the committee’s report by its chairman, Prof. Theodore Bala Maiyaki, who represents Qua’an-Pan South Constituency. Presenting the report, Maiyaki said, “The proposed constitutional amendment has become necessary in view of the security challenges facing the country, the manpower shortage in the Nigeria Police Force and the need to strengthen local policing arrangements.” Following deliberations, the lawmakers adopted the committee’s recommendations and voted in support of the proposed constitutional amendment. In Taraba, the state House of Assembly on Tuesday unanimously approved the constitutional amendment bill seeking to establish state police, marking a major legislative step toward decentralizing security and reinforcing crime prevention across the state. The bill, transmitted from the National Assembly as part of ongoing constitutional review processes, was formally laid before the lawmakers by the Majority Leader, Hon. Jethro Yakubu Zikengyu, and received by the Speaker, Rt. Hon. John Kizito Bonzena. Following exhaustive deliberations on the floor of the House, members unanimously voted to adopt the legislative measure, signaling strong backing for localized security architectures to tackle emerging criminal challenges. Speaking after the adoption, Speaker John Kizito Bonzena noted that establishing a state police system will drastically improve response times, foster closer intelligence sharing with federal security agencies, and create meaningful employment opportunities for youths. Bonzena said: “The proposed state police framework will strengthen our institutional capacity to curb criminal activities, protect rural and urban communities, and guarantee public safety across Taraba State.” In Zamfara State, the members of the state House of Assembly have passed the resolution supporting constitutional alterations aimed at facilitating the establishment of state police. The Speaker of the Assembly Hon. Bilyaminu Ismail Moriki, disclosed that the establishment of state police would complement the efforts of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal in addressing insecurity in the state and in across the country. Moriko expressed optimism that the Zamfara State Government would provide the necessary framework and support required to ensure the effective operation of state Police if established. “Our Governor Dauda Lawal Is committed to a peaceful Zamfara. That is why he assured of his total support to see this new development see the light of the day,” Moriki said Lawmakers in the Nasarawa State House of Assembly have also adopted the position of the NASS and passed the bill as sent to them by the national Assembly to establish state police in the state. The approval was given on Wednesday during plenary in Lafia, presided over by the Speaker, Dr. Danladi Jatau. Jatau read the 26 clauses of the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, transmitted by the National Assembly, before putting each clause to a voice vote. The state lawmakers unanimously voted in favour of all the clauses, after which the Speaker declared that the bill as passed into law. In a similar display of support for state police, the Yobe State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment establishing state police in Nigeria. The Speaker of the Yobe State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Chiroma Buba Mashio confirmed this to Vanguard correspondent on Thursday. Mashio signed the resolution on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. Yobe’s approval adds the state to those supporting decentralised policing amid persistent security challenges across the country. In the same vein, the Benue State House of Assembly has thrown its weight behind the establishment of state police in Nigeria, adopting a proposed constitutional amendment bill seeking to provide the legal framework for decentralised policing to tackle the country’s growing security challenges. The decision was taken during plenary presided over by the Speaker, Mr. Alfred Emberga, following deliberations on the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026. The Executive bill was presented for consideration by the House Majority Leader, Mr. Peter Ipusu, who urged lawmakers to give it accelerated consideration to ensure the legislative process was completed within the stipulated timeframe. The proposed amendment seeks to establish a constitutional framework for the creation and operation of state police services alongside the Federal Police Service, with provisions addressing their responsibilities, funding and operational guidelines. The House in a unanimous vote passed the constitutional amendment. The Speaker in his ruling directed the Clerk to convey the resolution of the House to the National Assembly. However, the bill is still facing deliberations in the Katsina State House of Assembly, after it took the first legislative step towards considering the proposed State Police Bill, following its receipt and passage through first reading. The development marks the beginning of the Assembly’s consideration of the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police and decentralise Nigeria’s policing system amid persistent security challenges. The same situation has played out at the Borno State House of Assembly, which is still deliberating on the state police bill after it received it from the NASS. The Clerk of the Borno State House of Assembly, Shettima Garba, confirmed that the House leadership is yet to deliberate nor pass the Police Bill into law. The clerk said however that had met and read out the bill at one of its plenary sessions. According to him, the bill needs ample time to study its positive or negative impact to the citizenry. In Jigawa State, the State House of Assembly has raised a committee to critically examine the constitutional amendments bill and make recommendations on how it reflects the interests of the people of Jigawa State. ‎The Speaker of Jigawa State House of Assembly, Haruna Dangyatim, said the Assembly had already received the bill and would work on it within the stipulated timeline. ‎Dangyatim said: “‎We have received the Constitution Amendment Bill from the National Assembly, and I want to assure you that we will do the needful before the deadline given to all state assemblies which is the end of this month. ‎“Within the stipulated timeline contained in the letter of the bill, we are given 30 days to complete the legislative work on the bill from the date we received the letter,” he stated. ‎The Speaker assured that the House would give the bill accelerated attention, saying that they were studying the document thoroughly to ensure that their position aligns with the aspirations of the people. ‎In Kano, the State House of Assembly has conducted the first reading of the proposed State Police Bill and distributed copies of the draft legislation to members for further study. The Chief Press Secretary and spokesperson of the Assembly, Kamal Sani Shawai, disclosed this to Vanguard on Thursday while explaining the status of the proposed bill. Shawai said copies of the draft had been given to lawmakers to enable them to study its provisions before the House reconvenes to deliberate on it. He said the Assembly would take further action on the bill after members had familiarised themselves with its contents. But in Adamawa, the assemblymen are yet to deliberate and take a position on the state police bill. The Chairman of the House Committee on Information, Hon Musa Kalam, however said that they members would soon meet to take action on the bill. A similar situation is playing out at the Bauchi State House of Assembly, which is yet to conclude consideration of the proposed State Police bill, despite the expiration of the two-week deadline given to an ad-hoc committee set up to examine the proposal. The Speaker of the House, Abubakar Y. Suleiman, had constituted the committee, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, Jamilu Ummaru Dahiru, to deliberate on the bill and report back to the whole house. However, two weeks after the committee was given the deadline to complete its assignment, the House is yet to announce the outcome of its deliberations or the passage of the bill. The delay leaves the proposed establishment of State Police in Bauchi State pending, amid growing calls for stronger security measures to tackle insecurity across the country. items.title: DSS secures 7th death sentence as Adamawa court convicts three over kidnap of Catholic priests
items.description: A high Court of Adamawa State, on Thursday, sentenced to death three persons who kidnapped two Catholic priests in February 2025. Delivering judgement, Justice Christopher Mapeo found the three men guilty of criminal conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, conspiracy to commit armed robbery, armed robbery, harboring a kidnapped person and negotiating to receive ransom for the release of Reverend Fathers Matthew Dutsemi and Abraham Sauman. The judge sentenced the three men, Taledo Demiel, Namomai Medan and Mikaila Yusuf, to death for kidnapping, armed robbery and other offences.Thursday’s death sentence is the seventh secured by the DSS this year. On 20th May, 2026, Ekiti High Court sentenced two men, Ibrahim Abubakar and Abdullahi Abubakar to death by hanging for kidnapping. About two weeks later, on 3rd June, 2026, a Federal High Court in Abuja sentenced to death by hanging, four men who, in June 2022, massacred scores of worshippers at the St. Francis Catholic church, Owo, Ondo State. The convicts are Idris Abdulmalik Omeiza, Alqasim Idris, Jamiu Abdulmalik and Abdulkareem Idris. Less than two weeks later, on 15th June, 2026, a Katsina High Court sentenced a female arms courier, Hauwa’u Mukhtar, to death by hanging. The following day, on 16th June, 2026, a Kogi High Court sentenced Jibrin Halilu to death by hanging for kidnapping and murdering his neighbour in Obajana, an industrial town in the state. About a week after the Kogi sentencing, on 22nd June, 2026, a Sokoto High court sentenced three persons Muhammed Yusuf Sallau, Jabbi Ahlaji Yale and Kabiru Muhammed, to death by hanging, for terrorism and for transporting arms. Less than three months later, on28th September 2026, a Sokoto High Court sentenced Ibrahim Usman aka Dan Iyali to death by hanging over his involvement in the killing of three kidnapped persons in the state. items.title: Damang Gold Mine Airport project to cost at least $80m —Community Relations Manager
items.description: Damang Gold Mine Limited’s Community Relations Manager, Ramy Oboro, has disclosed that the company’s planned airport in the Western Region is expected to cost at least US$80 million to complete. Speaking on a special edition of Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen programme in Tarkwa on Thursday, October 22, Mr Oboro said the estimated cost covered the initial preparation of the land and the construction of the supporting infrastructure required to make the airstrip operational. He explained that Phase One would involve levelling the land, while Phase Two would focus on constructing the additional facilities and installing the necessary equipment and electrical systems. These would include a pole to receive signals and other electrical equipment required for the airstrip’s operations. “It is anticipated that when we are done with the airport, it is going to cost us not less than 80 million dollars, both Phase One and Phase Two,” he said. READ ALSO: Damang to get an airport – Ibrahim Mahama announces after mine takeover Mr Oboro added that the final cost could exceed the US$80 million estimate, given the scope of the work and the infrastructure required to complete the project. “I think it will even go beyond that,” he said. Background Damang Gold Mine, formerly operated by Gold Fields Ghana Limited, was handed over to Engineers and Planners in April 2026 after the company won a competitive tender for the concession. The symbolic handover took place at the mine site on Saturday, April 18, 2026, with the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, overseeing the transfer. The process followed the expiration of Gold Fields’ lease, after which the government put the concession up for competitive tender supervised by the Minerals Commission. Business mogul and Chief Executive Officer of Engineers and Planners, Ibrahim Mahama, pledged significant infrastructure investments for communities around the Damang Mine following the company’s takeover of operations.

items.title: Damang Gold Mine to set aside portion of gold output for community development
items.description: Damang Gold Mine Ltd says it will set aside a portion of its gold production to finance development projects in its host communities through a community foundation fund. The company’s Community Relations Manager, Rammy Oboro, said the fund would accumulate over three years before management and traditional leaders jointly identify and prioritise projects for implementation. Speaking on a special edition of Asempa FM’s Ekosii Sen programme in Tarkwa-Damang, Mr Oboro said the arrangement was intended to ensure that communities affected by the mine’s operations benefit directly from its activities. He said the communities had been informed of the share of the fund allocated to them, based on the level of impact the mine’s operations had on each area. “For our foundation fund, we have agreed that for every ounce we produce, we will keep some for development. The catchment communities are aware of the percentage they will get, depending on the level of impact the company is getting from the community,” he said. Mr Oboro explained that the three-year accumulation period would allow the fund to grow before the company and traditional leaders agreed on priority projects. He added that the company intended to award contracts to people within the host communities to ensure that the economic benefits of the projects remained in the local areas. Local employment commitments Mr Oboro said the initiative formed part of measures introduced following the change in the mine’s management, with the Managing Director directing the Community Relations team to ensure that corporate social responsibility commitments were properly implemented. He said a corporate social responsibility forum with stakeholders had resulted in an agreement for 60 per cent of the mine’s workforce to be drawn from host communities, with the remaining 40 per cent open to other Ghanaians. The communities identified as part of the mine’s catchment area are Subri, Damang, Kyekyewere, Huni Valley, Amoanda, Koduakrom, Bompraasu, Twenda, Aboso and Mile 4 Nyamebekyere. Mr Oboro also mentioned a sub-community within Huni Valley as part of the areas with which the company engages. He said Damang Gold Mine remained committed to strengthening relations with its host communities and ensuring that its operations translated into tangible development benefits for residents.
