À Saly, la CPE passe sous présidence guinéenne et fixe le cap pour la gestion des barrages [Par Aboubacar Sakho]
items.description: La 156ᵉ réunion ordinaire de la Commission permanente des eaux (CPE) de l’Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS) s’est tenue les 20 et 21 octobre 2026 à Saly, au Sénégal. Cette rencontre a réuni les représentants des États membres, du Haut-Commissariat, du Comité de bassin, ainsi que des sociétés de gestion et d’exploitation des ouvrages communs, notamment la SOGED, la SOGEM, la SOGENAV et la SEMAF-SA. Au cœur des travaux figuraient le bilan de la gestion des barrages de Manantali, de Gouina, de Félou et de Diama, l’examen des programmes d’exploitation pour la fin de l’année 2026, ainsi que plusieurs enjeux environnementaux et agricoles liés à la gestion des ressources en eau du bassin du fleuve Sénégal. La cérémonie d’ouverture a été marquée par le passage de témoin entre le Sénégal et la Guinée à la tête de la Commission permanente des eaux. Conformément à l’article 8 du règlement intérieur de la CPE, amendé par la résolution n° 00407 du 21 décembre 2004, la République de Guinée assure désormais la présidence de cette instance pour une durée d’un an, succédant ainsi à la République du Sénégal. La passation s’est déroulée entre M. Moussa BERTHE, représentant le Coordonnateur de la Cellule nationale OMVS/OMVG du Sénégal, et Mme Hawa TRAORE, représentant le Coordonnateur de la Cellule nationale OMVS de Guinée. À cette occasion, les participants ont salué la qualité de la présidence sénégalaise et adressé leurs félicitations à l’équipe sortante. Ils ont également exprimé leurs encouragements à la Guinée pour la réussite de son nouveau mandat. Après les mots de bienvenue de M. Moussa BERTHE, le Secrétaire général de l’OMVS, M. Niokhor NDOUR, a félicité l’ensemble des acteurs du système pour leur implication constante dans les travaux de la Commission. Il a souligné le caractère déterminant de cet engagement collectif pour améliorer durablement la gestion des ressources en eau du bassin du fleuve Sénégal. La cérémonie a également été empreinte de recueillement à la suite du rappel à Dieu de M. Djibril NDAW, chauffeur mécanicien au Haut-Commissariat de l’OMVS. Des prières ont été formulées en sa mémoire. Les travaux ont permis d’examiner l’état d’exécution des recommandations des précédentes réunions, ainsi que le bilan du programme de gestion des barrages arrêté lors de la 155ᵉ réunion ordinaire de la CPE. À l’issue des échanges, la Commission a constaté que les programmes de gestion des barrages de Manantali, de Gouina, de Félou et de Diama avaient été globalement respectés. Pour le barrage de Manantali, les lâchers d’eau avaient notamment été programmés afin de garantir, à Bakel, des débits minimaux répondant aux besoins en aval, notamment pour l’agriculture, les consommations humaines et animales et la navigation. La réunion a également permis de faire le point sur les objectifs de production d’énergie hydroélectrique fixés pour 2026. Les productibles annuels adoptés s’élèvent à 915 GWh pour Manantali, 583,348 GWh pour Gouina et 299,462 GWh pour Félou. Ces objectifs traduisent la volonté de concilier les besoins en eau des populations et des activités économiques avec les impératifs de production énergétique, dans un contexte où la gestion coordonnée des ouvrages demeure essentielle à l’équilibre du bassin À l’issue de l’examen des propositions soumises par le Haut-Commissariat, la SOGED, la SOGEM et la SEMAF-SA, la CPE a adopté les programmes de gestion des barrages pour la période allant du 22 octobre au 31 décembre 2026. La Commission a par ailleurs examiné les présentations de la Direction nationale du génie rural de Guinée (DNGR), de l’Agence de développement rural de la vallée du fleuve Sénégal (ADRS), de la Société nationale pour le développement rural (SONADER) et de la Société nationale d’aménagement et d’exploitation des terres du delta du fleuve Sénégal et des vallées du fleuve Sénégal et de la Falémé (SAED). Ces communications ont porté sur les superficies mises en valeur et les productions agricoles de 2026, les prévisions d’emblavures pour 2027 ainsi que les mesures d’entretien des axes hydrauliques. En prenant acte des activités réalisées par les sociétés d’aménagement hydro-agricole, la CPE s’est félicitée des efforts accomplis et les a encouragées à consolider les acquis. Ces actions restent essentielles pour soutenir la production agricole, améliorer la maîtrise de l’eau et préserver le bon fonctionnement des infrastructures hydrauliques Au terme de deux jours de travaux, la 156ᵉ réunion ordinaire de la Commission permanente des eaux a permis de consolider les orientations relatives à la gestion coordonnée des barrages, à la production hydroélectrique et à la préservation des ressources naturelles du bassin. La prochaine réunion de la CPE est prévue à Conakry, en Guinée, au cours de la deuxième quinzaine de décembre 2026. Elle se tiendra sous la présidence guinéenne, dans la continuité des efforts engagés par les États membres et les structures de l’OMVS pour une gestion concertée, durable et solidaire des eaux du fleuve Sénégal. Aboubacar SAKHO Expert en Communication au Haut-Commissariat de l’OMVS à Dakar L’article À Saly, la CPE passe sous présidence guinéenne et fixe le cap pour la gestion des barrages [Par Aboubacar Sakho] est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Drame au foyer universitaire de Sidi Mansour | Grève générale à l’appel de l’Uget
items.description: L’Union générale des étudiants de Tunisie (Uget) a annoncé une grève générale ce vendredi 23 octobre 2026 dans l'ensemble des facultés et instituts supérieurs du gouvernorat de Sfax, suite du décès tragique de l'étudiante Rahma Dziri, survenu au sein du foyer universitaire de Sidi Mansour. Inscrite à l’Institut supérieur des études technologiques (Iset) de Sfax, la jeune fille a été victime d’un malaise dans la nuit du mercredi 21 octobre dernier. D'après les témoignages de ses camarades, la prise en charge médicale aurait souffert d'un retard conséquent, l’ambulance ne serait arrivée sur les lieux que plus d'une heure après le premier appel d’urgence. Face à cette situation, l'organisation étudiante appelle à une mobilisation générale pour exiger l'instauration de structures médicales permanentes au sein des résidences universitaires. Dans son communiqué, l'UGET réclame des solutions durables pour garantir l'accès immédiat aux soins et exhorte les autorités de tutelle à assumer leurs responsabilités en prenant des mesures d'urgence pour préserver la vie des étudiants. items.title: African business leaders, diplomats and industry giants converge for 2026 Africa Business Forum & Awards
items.description: Business excellence, investment diplomacy, entrepreneurship and African cultural identity took centre stage at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City in Accra on Saturday, 17 October 2026, as distinguished business leaders, entrepreneurs, investors, diplomats and corporate executives gathered for the Africa Business Forum & Awards 2026. Held under the theme “Shaping Africa’s Business Future: From a Single African Market to Global Competitiveness,” the continental gathering celebrated outstanding business achievements while promoting stronger commercial relationships, investment opportunities and strategic partnerships across African markets. Powered by KN Unique Communications, a subsidiary of KN Communications Group, the event combined high-level business engagement with an awards gala recognising exceptional companies, entrepreneurs, business executives and institutions contributing to Africa’s economic transformation. Distinguished Diplomats and AfCFTA Officials Grace the Occasion Among the distinguished personalities at the gathering was H.E. Rui Pedro Afonso Livramento, Chief of Staff of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat, whose participation highlighted the importance of regional economic integration and stronger commercial cooperation among African countries. The presence of the AfCFTA Secretariat’s Chief of Staff was particularly significant given the forum’s theme, which reflected Africa’s ambition to strengthen intra-African trade, expand market access and position African businesses to compete more effectively in international markets. H.E. Selestine Gervas Kakele, High Commissioner of Tanzania to Ghana, was among the diplomatic representatives associated with the event. Tanzanian media reported his remarks encouraging African businesses and investors to explore opportunities in Tanzania. The participation of these diplomatic personalities reinforced the forum’s objective of creating meaningful connections between governments, investors, entrepreneurs and private-sector institutions. KN Communications Group CEO Highlights Vision for African Business Excellence Mr Oheneba Kwabena Kena, Chief Executive Officer of KN Communications Group, Board Member of the Africa Business and Trade Council, and Event Director of the Africa Business Forum & Awards 2026, was among the prominent business leaders at the gathering. Through KN Unique Communications, a subsidiary of KN Communications Group, the event provided a platform for recognising business achievements, encouraging professional engagement and facilitating relationships among businesses operating across African markets. The initiative reflected the organising company’s commitment to promoting African business excellence, celebrating entrepreneurship and creating opportunities for stronger commercial cooperation. The forum brought together stakeholders from different sectors to exchange ideas on investment, innovation, entrepreneurship, leadership and the opportunities emerging from Africa’s increasingly interconnected markets. Business Leaders Explore Investment and Cross-Border Opportunities Through CEO conversations and the Country Invest – Diplomat Series, participants engaged in discussions concerning business expansion, investment opportunities, institutional cooperation and the conditions necessary for sustainable economic growth. The forum also provided opportunities for business leaders to interact with diplomatic representatives, industry executives and potential partners from other African countries. Speakers from various Countries were among the personalities whose contributions to discussions surrounding the gathering drew attention to business governance, regulatory institutions and fair competition. Outstanding African Companies and Business Leaders Recognised The awards gala celebrated organisations and individuals contributing to Africa’s development across banking, insurance, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, shipping, financial technology, tourism and other sectors. Among the recognised companies were Prime Bank of Kenya, Hapag-Lloyd Ghana Limited, Happy Sunshine Company Limited, Vanguard Assurance Company Limited, B5 Plus Company Limited, Enterprise Trustees Limited, G-Force Employment Solutions, Labianca Company Limited, JUMO Ghana Limited, Epiroc Equipment Ghana Limited and Tobinco Pharmaceuticals Limited. Distinguished individual honourees included Dame Dr Adaora Umeoji, Group Managing Director of Zenith Bank Plc; Dr Rasik Kantaria, Founder of Prime Bank; Luísa Patrícia Agostinho, Chief Executive Officer of Muatu Bridge Capital; and other business executives whose achievements reflect the diversity and strength of African enterprise. Tanzania’s Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority also received recognition for sustainable tourism and conservation management, with Conservation Commissioner Abdul-Razak Badru highlighting the importance of protecting natural and cultural heritage while promoting responsible tourism development. African Culture and Business Networking Take Centre Stage Beyond the business forum and awards presentations, the gathering featured an evening of African cultural performances, live entertainment and a gala dinner. The cultural activities complemented the business discussions, providing delegates with opportunities to network, celebrate African identity and strengthen professional relationships. The combination of diplomatic engagement, corporate recognition and cultural expression highlighted the relationship between Africa’s economic ambitions and its rich cultural heritage. Building a More Connected and Competitive African Economy The Africa Business Forum & Awards 2026 reinforced the importance of business leadership, entrepreneurship, investment diplomacy and strategic partnerships in advancing Africa’s economic transformation. The participation of representatives from the AfCFTA Secretariat, diplomatic missions, private-sector organisations and business institutions demonstrated the relevance of collaborative platforms in strengthening commercial relationships across national borders. As African businesses continue to explore opportunities presented by regional economic integration, initiatives such as the Africa Business Forum & Awards provide a platform for celebrating achievement, exchanging knowledge and fostering partnerships. The Africa Business Forum & Awards 2026 was powered by KN Unique Communications, a subsidiary of KN Communications Group.

items.title: Spain refers LaLiga chief to tribunal over Real Madrid Nazi comments
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye LaLiga president Javier Tebas has been referred to Spain’s sports tribunal over his comparison of Real Madrid’s communication tactics to Nazi propaganda, following the Spanish club’s demand for his resignation. According to Reuters, Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) announced on Thursday that it had referred Tebas to the Administrative Court for Sport (TAD) to determine whether his remarks breached regulations protecting sporting dignity and decorum. The referral concerns comments Tebas made on social media on October 16, criticising Real Madrid’s handling of complaints about refereeing decisions and the club’s television coverage of match officials. Tebas accused Real Madrid of using communication tactics that recalled propaganda methods employed by Joseph Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister. Real Madrid subsequently demanded the immediate resignation of the 64-year-old, describing his comparison as unacceptable for someone holding the position of LaLiga president. However, Tebas insisted that he was referring to propaganda techniques rather than Nazi ideology or Real Madrid’s supporters. In its referral, the CSD asked the tribunal to assess whether the remarks could constitute a serious offence under Article 76.4.b of Spain’s 1990 Sports Law, which covers public acts that infringe upon sporting dignity or decorum. Possible sanctions for such offences include warnings, fines or suspension. The controversy followed Tebas’s criticism of Real Madrid’s efforts to challenge the standard of refereeing in Spanish football. The club has repeatedly questioned officiating decisions through its in-house television channel. In a fresh post on X on Thursday, Tebas defended his comments and questioned why Real Madrid’s accusations against Spanish referees had not attracted similar scrutiny under the rules governing sporting dignity. “Defending the competition also requires responding to those who constantly discredit it,” Tebas wrote, adding that he intended to continue exercising that responsibility. He also argued that Real Madrid’s repeated questioning of the integrity of Spanish football could itself be examined under the same rules. The AFP also reports that the CSD emphasised the importance of protecting respect, coexistence and fair play in sport. The tribunal will determine whether the matter warrants disciplinary proceedings. No finding of wrongdoing against Tebas has been announced. items.title: Sudan lifts ban on 46 imports as inflation rises and Dollar hits SDG 10,300
items.description: Sudan has lifted import restrictions on 46 goods as the Dollar climbs to SDG 10,300 and annual inflation reaches 28.29%, deepening pressure on consumers already struggling with soaring food prices. Sudan’s Sovereignty Council chairman Abdelfattah El Burhan has cancelled a cabinet decision banning imports of 46 goods, as Sudan’s currency and consumers remain under pressure from rising prices. Finance minister Jibril Ibrahim says the decision takes account of consumers’ needs while providing measures to protect domestic producers. Traders and consumers have reported an immediate fall in some prices following the announcement. Vegetables at Khartoum Central Market (File photo: Supplied) The National Importers’ Chamber welcomed the move but called for Prime Minister Kamil Idris to issue a clear, enforceable decision cancelling Resolution No. 74, which introduced the restrictions. The chamber’s chairman, El Sadiq Jalal El Din Saleh, said the import ban had disrupted markets and caused substantial losses to importers. However, foreign-exchange dealers reported that the Dollar rose on Thursday to SDG 10,200 for buying and SDG 10,300 for selling, an increase of SDG 100 from Wednesday. Experts expect further increases, particularly following the lifting of the import restrictions. Inflation and food prices rise Sudan’s annual inflation rate rose to 28.29% in September, up from 26.14% in August, while monthly inflation reached 7.5%, according to the Central Bureau of Statistics. Food and drink prices rose by 17.26% during the month, with annual inflation in the category reaching 36.81%. Annual inflation was significantly higher in urban areas, at 40.35%, than in rural areas, at 21.18%. War compounds economic crisis Economists attribute rising inflation to the destruction of Sudan’s productive base during the war, growing dependence on imports, the depreciation of the pound, and the use of the customs Dollar to calculate duties. Taxes, customs charges, and transport costs have added to the burden. The conflict has also prevented many people from returning to agricultural and other productive areas, restricting domestic supplies. Markets remain fragmented between areas controlled by the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, while production and supply chains have yet to recover. The latest figures point to a difficult economic balance: easing import restrictions may improve the availability of goods, but the continuing rise in the Dollar and the cost of food threaten to erode any relief for consumers. items.title: Pharma : pourquoi le Royaume séduit les laboratoires allemands
items.description: Accès au marché, partenaires industriels, souplesse du régime d’importation : l’agence allemande GTAI place le Royaume devant l’Algérie et la Tunisie, que les laboratoires de son pays veuillent vendre, fabriquer sur place ou approvisionner d’autres marchés africains. Vendre des médicaments finis, les fabriquer pour le marché local ou produire pour d’autres pays africains : les options des laboratoires allemands ne sont pas les mêmes à Rabat, Alger ou Tunis. Dans une analyse récente, Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI), l’agence fédérale allemande de promotion du commerce extérieur et des investissements, donne l’avantage au Royaume. Signée de ses correspondants à Tunis et à Casablanca, Verena Matschoß et Ullrich Umann, l’étude y voit le terrain d’accueil le plus propice des trois pays, doté de l’appareil industriel et logistique le plus solide pour servir le reste du continent. GTAI avance trois atouts : des fabricants locaux capables de produire sous licence ou à façon, des circuits de distribution structurés et un régime d’importation plus souple qu’en Algérie, moins exposé aux impayés qu’en Tunisie. Ces points forts valent surtout pour l’exportation de médicaments finis et pour la fabrication destinée au marché intérieur, avec la possibilité de réexporter depuis une usine installée dans le pays. Le choix du site reste toutefois dicté par la nature des médicaments, les coûts industriels, les autorisations et les pays de destination. Le marché pèse 25,9 milliards de dirhams (environ 2,4 milliards d’euros) en 2024, selon des données du Conseil de la concurrence citées par l’agence. Il demeure largement alimenté de l’extérieur : 10,6 milliards de dirhams d’importations contre 1,6 milliard d’exportations, soit un déficit de neuf milliards. Le pays compte 56 établissements industriels, 66 grossistes et plus de 14.000 pharmacies, un maillage qui permet aux laboratoires étrangers de s’adosser à des acteurs en place avant d’envisager leurs propres usines. Sothema, Cooper Pharma et Maphar figurent parmi les partenaires possibles. L’Allemagne y est déjà bien placée. Elle était en 2024 le premier fournisseur du Royaume pour les produits du chapitre 30 de la nomenclature douanière, avec près de 18 % des importations, grâce aux vaccins et aux produits sanguins, la France gardant la tête pour les médicaments finis. La demande bénéficie de l’élargissement de l’assurance maladie, mais les prix réglementés et le poids des génériques limitent les marges. Toute importation passe en outre par un établissement pharmaceutique industriel agréé et par l’aval de l’Agence marocaine des médicaments et des produits de santé. L’Algérie suit une logique inverse, celle de la substitution aux importations. Avec 233 établissements de production, dont 138 fabricants de médicaments, elle couvrait 83 % de ses besoins en février 2026, d’après l’Agence nationale des produits pharmaceutiques. L’importation d’un produit déjà fabriqué localement y est restreinte, et les opérateurs doivent obtenir agrément, enregistrement et approbation d’un programme d’importation. Depuis fin avril, le dépôt de nouvelles demandes d’agrément est suspendu, une mesure encore en vigueur fin septembre à la connaissance de GTAI. Médicaments innovants, produits complexes, principes actifs et transferts de technologie y conservent des débouchés, mais une implantation industrielle ou un partenaire local s’impose souvent. La Tunisie compte une quarantaine d’usines, qui couvrent environ 80 % des besoins en volume et 60 % en valeur, surtout grâce aux génériques. Ses fabricants exportent près de 18 % de leur production vers 35 pays, selon l’Agence de promotion de l’investissement extérieur. Le risque tient aux paiements : la Pharmacie centrale de Tunisie, pivot des importations, règle avec douze à treize mois de retard. GTAI cite en exemple l’accord conclu en février 2026 entre Sanofi et le groupe Kilani, qui confie à Teriak la fabrication locale d’une partie du portefeuille du laboratoire français et à Medicis certaines activités de visite médicale et de commercialisation. The post Pharma : pourquoi le Royaume séduit les laboratoires allemands appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Residents praise Ibrahim Mahama over Damang Mine’s road projects, call for more jobs for women
items.description: Residents of Damang in the Tarkwa-Nsuaem Municipality of the Western Region have praised Damang Gold Mine Ltd for developments in the community since it took over operations six months ago, while calling for more employment opportunities for women and National Service personnel. Speaking on a special edition of Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen programme in Tarkwa on Thursday, October 22, the residents said they had witnessed positive changes since the mine’s management changed. One resident commended the new management but appealed to subcontractors working with the mine to engage more National Service personnel. The resident argued that they should be given opportunities to serve at the mine rather than being posted mainly to government institutions, where allowances are lower. Another resident praised Engineers and Planners Chief Executive Officer Ibrahim Mahama for road construction projects, saying the improved roads had made journeys to Kumasi easier and less tiring. “I would like to appreciate Mr Ibrahim Mahama for the construction of roads. At first, whenever I was going to Kumasi, it was very tiring, but now it is much easier,” the resident said. A third resident also expressed gratitude for the developments but urged the company to create more jobs for women. “Looking at the latest developments within the Damang community within six months of operations by Damang Gold Mine, we are really grateful to Mr Ibrahim Mahama, but we are pleading with them to employ more ladies in the company,” the resident said. Background Damang Gold Mine, formerly operated by Gold Fields Ghana Limited, was handed over to Engineers and Planners in April 2026 after the company won a competitive tender for the concession. The symbolic handover took place at the mine site on Saturday, April 18, 2026, with the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, overseeing the transfer. The process followed the expiration of Gold Fields’ lease, after which the government put the concession up for competitive tender supervised by the Minerals Commission.

items.title: Burkina: 2 800 milliards FCFA pour «l’Énergie pour Tous» dans 10 ans
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 22 octobre 2026). Le Conseil des Ministres s'est réuni ce jeudi, sous la présidence du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, Président du Faso, Chef de l'État, Président du Conseil des Ministres. Selon le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias TRAORÉ assurant l’Intérim du Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, le Conseil a délibéré sur les dossiers inscrits à son ordre du jour et pris des décisions importantes pour la bonne marche de la Nation, conformément aux orientations de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). Pour le compte de la Présidence du Faso, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création de l'Initiative Présidentielle Énergie pour Tous « Faso Wa-Fulu », en langue nationale san. Portée par le Ministère en charge de l'Énergie, cette initiative d'envergure nationale vise à garantir un accès généralisé à l'électricité d'ici à 2030. D’un coût de plus de 2 800 milliards FCFA sur 10 ans, le programme s'articule autour de 4 composantes que sont les Brigades d'électrification, l’Inclusion communautaire, l’Accès énergétique et la Souveraineté énergétique. « Cette initiative vise à accélérer l’accès de l'énergie pour tous à l'horizon 2030. C'est une initiative qui va s'étaler sur une période de 10 ans, avec une première période d'accélération de la prise en charge des questions énergétiques et une seconde phase de 5 ans qui sera consacrée à la consolidation des acquis », a expliqué le Ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, le Camarade Yacouba Zabré GOUBA. Naissance de la Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB) Au titre du Ministère de l'Industrie, du Commerce et de l'Artisanat, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création d’une société d'économie mixte à participation publique majoritaire dénommée Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB). Pour le Ministre du Commerce, de l'Industrie et de l'Artisanat, le Camarade Serge Gnaniodem PODA, cette société d'économie mixte est dotée d'un capital initial d’un milliard FCFA avec une participation de 45 % pour l’État, 10 % pour BRAFASO et 45 % pour le secteur privé burkinabè. « La SOVIB permettra la création de centaines d’emplois et la transformation de vignes produites au Burkina Faso », a soutenu le Ministre PODA. Cette unité industrielle sera basée à Bobo-Dioulasso, et nécessitera un investissement d'environ 9,8 milliards FCFA. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso L’article Burkina: 2 800 milliards FCFA pour «l’Énergie pour Tous» dans 10 ans est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: DSS arrests 23-year-old female arms courier in Nasarawa
items.description: — Sule commends security agencies over crackdown on arms trafficking By Edwin Philip LAFIA — Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, has commended the Department of State Services (DSS) for its sustained efforts to clamp down on gun runners and arms traffickers in the state following the arrest of a 23-year-old female suspected arms courier in Keffi. The governor’s commendation was contained in a statement issued on Thursday by his Press Secretary, Ibrahim Addra, who described the arrest of Aisha Mohammed, a resident of Bwari, Federal Capital Territory, as a significant breakthrough. According to the statement, Mohammed was arrested with 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition and three empty magazines. “The suspect, currently in custody, was arrested while in possession of 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition with three empty magazines,” the statement said. It added that other suspected arms couriers arrested between August and September 2026 included Hassan Sani, 40; Abdulkadir Idrissa, 41; and Salihu Garba, 70, also known as Nabayi. The statement said security operatives recovered 678 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, 99 rounds of 7.5mm ammunition and other items from the suspects. It further disclosed that an alleged arms courier, Ismail Lawalli, a native of Zamfara State, was arrested in August along the Keffi-Abuja highway with 1,262 assorted rounds of ammunition. Sule praised DSS personnel and other security agencies in Nasarawa for their dedication and commitment to tackling arms trafficking and other criminal activities. He also commended the collaboration between the security agencies and his administration, pledging continued government support for their operations. The governor assured residents of his administration’s resolve to combat criminality and called on the public to support security agencies in maintaining peace and safety across the state. items.title: 2027: Momoh warns politicians against divisive rhetoric
items.description: — Says ethnic, religious appeals can turn neighbours into suspects By Olayinka Ajayi The Chairman of Channels Media Group, Dr John Momoh, has urged political parties and their supporters to avoid divisive rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that appeals to ethnicity and religion could deepen mistrust and threaten national unity. Momoh said political disagreements should not be allowed to degenerate into hostility, stressing that opponents should not be portrayed as enemies of the country. He spoke on Thursday while delivering the keynote address, titled Narratives That Build Nations in Diversity: Public Relations Leadership and the Future of Nigeria, at the 38th Dr Sam Epelle Gold Paper Lecture in Yola, Adamawa State. The event also featured the unveiling of Governor Ahmadu Fintiri as patron of the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR). Momoh said the approaching elections had heightened political competition, with parties building alliances, candidates making claims and supporters mobilising voters. “Democracy needs vigorous debate. It needs disagreement, scrutiny and the freedom to challenge those who govern. But disagreement should not become permission to dehumanise. Political opponents are not enemies of the nation,” he said. He warned that false allegations, manipulated videos and fabricated quotations could spread before those affected had an opportunity to respond, potentially hardening public opinion and fuelling divisions. “A divisive appeal to ethnicity or religion can turn a neighbour into a suspect,” he said. The media executive urged political leaders and other public figures to use their influence to calm tensions, reject language that could incite violence and correct false claims circulated by their supporters. He said the responsibility for maintaining a healthy political environment extended beyond candidates and parties to citizens, the media and other public institutions. Economic communication must reflect reality On the economy, Momoh said public confidence in government policies depended on whether citizens could feel the benefits in their daily lives. He noted that households continued to assess economic conditions through the cost of food, transportation, rent, school fees, electricity and healthcare. While citing figures he attributed to the World Bank and the Central Bank of Nigeria, Momoh said economic indicators showing growth or easing inflation should be explained alongside the realities facing households. He cited reported real GDP growth of 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026 and a decline in year-on-year headline inflation to 14.63 per cent in September from 15.39 per cent in August. Momoh cautioned that a decline in the inflation rate did not necessarily mean that prices had fallen, but could indicate that prices were rising more slowly. “If an official says that inflation has eased, and a family hears that food is still more expensive, the family is not being unreasonable. The two statements can both be true,” he said. He argued that effective public communication required government officials to explain economic developments honestly while continuing to address the impact of policies on citizens. “Growth must mean more than a number. It must become decent jobs, dependable public services, wages that can support a household, opportunity for young people, and confidence that the effort to build a life is worthwhile,” he said. Security requires public trust On security, Momoh identified insurgency, banditry, kidnapping, communal conflicts and farmer-pastoralist tensions among the challenges confronting communities across the country. He said insecurity in Adamawa and the wider North-East had disrupted homes, farming, education, livelihoods and family life. Momoh urged the government to strengthen security agencies through improved intelligence, equipment, training and coordination, while ensuring that communities had confidence in the authorities. “Behind every statistic is a person: a child who cannot attend school, a farmer afraid to return to a field, a family forced from its home, a community unable to reach a clinic. Their experience must not be reduced to a talking point in a political argument,” he said. He added that effective security required more than operational responses, stressing the importance of prevention, justice and public cooperation. “A government’s account of security will be judged by whether people can live, work, travel, learn and sleep without fear,” he said. According to him, honest communication should acknowledge difficult realities, identify responsibility and explain what is being done to address the problems. Momoh urges accountability in governance The Channels Media Group chairman also called on political leaders to match their public statements and promises with tangible results. He said citizens judged governments by their lived experiences rather than official announcements about reforms, development and improved services. “When leaders promise a road, citizens watch to see whether it is built. When the government promises relief, people ask whether it reaches those who need it,” he said. Momoh maintained that communication could not compensate for poorly designed policies or decisions taken without considering their consequences for the people. He urged leaders to seek honest advice before making decisions, assess who would benefit or suffer from proposed policies and explain the trade-offs involved. He also called for greater accountability, saying public officials should acknowledge delays, explain service failures and correct inaccurate claims rather than conceal mistakes. “A leader’s willingness to repair a mistake can strengthen trust more than pretending the mistake never happened,” he said. items.title: England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase in Rawalpindi clash
items.description: England’s Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare in Rawalpindi on Thursday. The 27-year-old captain rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India’s Shubman Gill. In the process, Brook also eclipsed England’s highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes. Brook’s scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England’s innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage. England’s captain Harry Brook celebrates after scoring a double century (200 runs) during the one-day international (ODI) tri-series cricket match between England and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 22, 2026. — AFP He made 202 from 116 deliveries, peppering the Sri Lanka attack with 21 fours and 10 sixes before departing to warm applause from the crowd. The defeat leaves England bottom of the standings after losing both their matches, with Brook saying they need to win their next two games to reach the final in Lahore. “Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn’t matter now. I thought we were going to be in a good position but, unfortunately, it doesn’t even count,” Brook said. “Heart-breaking. I think you’ve hit the nail on the head there. It’s very disappointing that we haven’t been able to defend 430, but that’s life, that’s cricket,” he added. “You don’t see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka. They’ve played exceptionally well. We couldn’t execute our skills enough with the ball and, again, they’ve just played an absolute blinder there. “We’ll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. We’ve got a good opportunity in the next couple of games to really try and get to that final in Lahore.” Joe Root provided strong support with 69 off 66 balls as England piled up 429-4. But the total proved insufficient as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake top-scored with 130 from 106 deliveries, while opener Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both fell three runs short of centuries. Sri Lanka’s Pavan Rathnayake in action in the one-day international (ODI) tri-series cricket match between England and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 22, 2026. — Reuters Needing six runs from the final two deliveries, Sri Lanka sealed victory when Liyanage launched Josh Tongue over long-off for six, leaving Brook’s record-breaking innings all in vain. Tongue was England’s most successful bowler with 3-79. England lost by 87 runs at the same venue in Rawalpindi on Tuesday to Pakistan, who lead the table with two wins from two.

items.title: Police begins training of 10,000 officers for 2027 polls
items.description: — Disu warns personnel against partisanship, electoral offences By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Nigeria Police Force has commenced training for 10,000 officers nationwide on election security management ahead of the 2027 general elections, with Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, charging personnel to remain neutral, professional and accountable. The five-day training programme, organised in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Trust Fund (NPTF), was formally inaugurated at the Nigeria Police Resource Centre, Jabi, Abuja, on Thursday. According to a statement by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, the programme is being conducted across designated centres and covers election security management, crowd control, conflict prevention, rules of engagement, human rights, intelligence gathering and lawful responses to election-related incidents. “The first phase brings together officers across 18 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with the training designed to ensure uniform operational standards ahead of nationwide deployment,” the statement said. Addressing participants, Disu said security was fundamental to credible elections, stressing that officers deployed for electoral duties must protect voters, electoral officials and the electoral process without fear or favour. He warned that any officer who compromised the neutrality of the Force would be held accountable. The IGP also directed police commands to strengthen intelligence gathering, operational planning and inter-agency coordination, particularly in areas affected by terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence. He warned against political violence, voter intimidation, ballot-box snatching, vote-buying and other electoral offences, saying offenders would be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law. Disu further announced plans for a dedicated 24-hour complaints line through which members of the public could report misconduct by officers deployed for election duties. He urged political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct peaceful campaigns, while calling on the media and civil society organisations to verify information before disseminating it. Speaking at the event, the Executive Secretary of the Nigeria Police Trust Fund, Mohammed Sheidu, reaffirmed the Fund’s commitment to supporting police preparedness through training, operational equipment and mobility. Sheidu said the initiative was aimed at equipping officers to remain disciplined, impartial and responsive throughout the electoral process. The ceremony was attended by Rear Admiral Sadiq Malafa (retd.), representing the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission; Afam O. Okeke, General Secretary of the Nigerian Bar Association; Brigadier-General J.A. Ifeanyi, representing the Chief of Army Staff; and Group Captain Yakubu Yusuf, representing the Chief of Air Staff. Also present were Deputy Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Zakari Ibrahim, representing the Commandant-General; Sheidu; members of the Force Management Team; and other senior police officers. The Nigeria Police Force said it remained committed to sustained training, intelligence-led planning, inter-agency collaboration and professional, impartial policing to provide a safe environment for Nigerians to exercise their electoral rights in 2027. items.title: A Congressional Race That’s a Referendum on the War
items.description: J ohn Quillin thought America’s Middle Eastern wars were safely in the past. He spent two decades in the Navy, enlisting not long before the September 11 attacks and retiring as a chief petty officer about 18 months after the United States withdrew from Afghanistan. “Now we’re right back in it,” he told me, “and it’s taking a huge toll on everybody.” I met Quillin as he handed out Democratic sample ballots outside an early-voting location in Chesapeake, Virginia. He is one of more than 80,000 veterans—along with more than 30,000 active-duty and reserve personnel—who live in Virginia’s Second Congressional District, where the debate over the Iran war is about far more than rising gas prices. The district wraps around Naval Station Norfolk, home of the Navy’s Fleet Forces Command. Since 2008, the seat has toggled between the major parties four times, and the results have mirrored overall House control. Polls show a tight race with money pouring in from both sides. Both Jen Kiggans, the Republican incumbent, and Elaine Luria, the Democratic challenger, are veterans who have centered their campaigns on the military, but in very different ways. Luria, a former Navy commander, is telling voters that the conflict in Iran has needlessly weakened the military and is endangering strategic goals in other parts of the world. Iran is a war of choice, she argues, that is taking a toll on service members through extended deployments, even as costs balloon and the timeline for bringing it to a close keeps shifting. People are worried about their friends and family members on active duty, she told me, and are “concerned about the fact that we are running the fleet into the ground.” Kiggans, a former naval-helicopter pilot, presents herself as a candidate who can work with the opposing party, and she has broken with the administration to champion an offshore wind development. But she is putting no distance between herself and Trump on the war, echoing his insistence that America must prevent Iran from having a nuclear weapon. Kiggans told the Associated Press last week that Luria has “chosen the side of Iran” and that “it’s like the Democrats are now siding with the Iranians and not standing with our military.” Many Republican voters in the district told me they agree with her support for Trump’s war, and are willing to endure temporary hardships if it means long-term success. Lance Lesher, a Navy veteran and the chairman of the Republican Party of Virginia Beach, told me that Iran has been at war with the United States since the country’s 1979 revolution—and that Trump was right to act when he did. “I mean, high prices for gasoline—no one likes that,” the 59-year-old Lesher told me. “I think most people, though, at least most older people, have the perspective—is it worth it? Is it worth paying $5 a gallon for gasoline for six months for Iran to not have a nuclear weapon?” L uria is wagering that undecided voters who are now paying more to fill their gas tanks and grocery carts won’t agree with that premise. At a meet and greet in Suffolk, Elisha Harris, a pioneering local football coach, started a call-and-response that summed up Luria’s pitch: “Gas was three-fifty. Now it’s over four. Diesel hit a record. We can’t take much more. Every fill-up’s a drain—” “It ain’t been the same, without Elaine!” the crowd responded. [ Read: Trump is considering a plan to strike Iran before the midterms ] Luria was first elected in 2018, turning the district blue amid an anti-Trump wave. She held the seat two years later, but Kiggans then beat her by three points in 2022 after tying the Democrat to the Biden administration’s disastrous withdrawal from Afghanistan. Luria is now hoping to return the favor, by capitalizing on the unpopularity of Trump’s foreign policy. Kiggans sits on the House Armed Services Committee, which has not held a public hearing on the Iran war since May 19. Calls for greater House oversight surged this spring amid reports of deteriorating conditions aboard aircraft carriers, including the Norfolk-based USS Gerald Ford, which took part in the opening days of the conflict. The carrier returned to Virginia in May after an 11-month deployment that was beset by plumbing issues and a fire that left hundreds of sailors without a place to sleep. When asked in March about the ship’s reported maintenance issues, Kiggans told a local news station that she was concerned about them, but that “this is not Carnival Cruise—this is the U.S. Navy.” It’s a line Luria repeats often, claiming that Kiggans has failed to provide oversight as the war degrades military readiness and needlessly endangers lives. “I know the number of veterans in this room who have served in uniform, like I have. And we have our sailors deploying in harm’s way,” Luria told the crowd in Suffolk. “The lack of sensitivity and compassion, her inability, on the Armed Services Committee, to stand up and ask tough questions of our military leadership—I mean, the silence is deafening.” The idea that Congress has abdicated oversight of the military repeatedly came up in my conversations with Democratic voters across the district. Many said that they were proud of their service and hold the military in the highest regard, but that patriotism also means criticizing the country and pointing out its mistakes. Mike Carter, who spent years flying F/A-18 Super Hornets, told me he’d come to the Luria event because he worried that the military and country were losing global respect. Marsha Simmons, who cast an early ballot for Luria, told me that her husband served in the Navy, and she worried that today’s Department of Defense was not taking national security seriously enough. Donna Grieco said that she loved her eight years working as a Navy nurse, and that the experience made her especially concerned about the long deployments sailors are enduring. “I don’t agree with the war,” she told me. “And I feel like the demands we are putting on our sailors—it’s not necessary.” N ot every veteran sees it that way. Over Mike Cassidy’s 22-year Navy career, he sailed the Baltic Sea and helped fight ISIS. He was deployed five times to the Persian Gulf. Cassidy’s service convinced him that American adversaries such as Iran need to be confronted. “I know what we’ve been up against in that part of the world,” he told me at a Republican Party barbecue. “I can tell you that we’re doing the right thing.” [ Read: Trump is preparing for a long war ] At 9 a.m. on a Saturday, the Lockside Bar and Grill in Chesapeake was packed with people decked out in glittery hats and red, white, and blue. Kiggans stood at a podium flanked by two American flags. “My oldest just had his first flight in an F/A-18 this week!” she announced. People whooped. “So many of us have family members that serve, and have kids that we’re leaving this great country to,” she went on. “It is the greatest country in the world. We’ve got to keep it that way.” At times, the rally seemed less about Kiggans than about Trump. His core supporters cheered when Representative Jim Jordan of Ohio took the stage and recited a list of MAGA world’s greatest hits: the Steele dossier, Jack Smith, Fani Willis. “Thanks for helping the president,” Jordan said to applause. “Talk about someone doing what he said he would do.” Kiggans has voted six times against resolutions that would have directed Trump to end the war with Iran. She declined an interview request, but in April, she said on a conservative talk-radio show that she “couldn’t be a stauncher supporter” of military action against Iran. When I asked the campaign whether she still held that position, Kiggans said in a statement that she wants the war to end quickly, but “Iran has been an enemy of the United States for decades and has been the sponsor of terrorism and terrorists around the world who have killed or injured thousands of Americans. Iran can never be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.” The race will likely hinge on a small number of voters who have not yet made up their mind. Kiggans knows this and has avoided uncomfortable questions about how the war is going. At an event in Virginia Beach this month with U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Kiggans was asked by a reporter if the war has had an impact on her campaign. A staff member quickly cut in: “We’re not going to talk about that.” *Illustration sources: Peter Casey / The Virginian-Pilot / Tribune News Service / Getty; Nathan Howard / Getty; AFP / Getty; Atta Kenare / AFP / Getty.

items.title: Myrtilles : le Maroc intègre le top 5 des fournisseurs de la Suisse
items.description: Pour la première fois, le Maroc figure parmi les cinq premiers fournisseurs de myrtilles fraîches du marché suisse. Au cours de la campagne de commercialisation 2025-2026, ses exportations vers ce pays ont bondi de 75 % par rapport à la saison précédente, selon les données rapportées par la plateforme spécialisée dans les marchés agricoles EastFruit . Entre juillet 2025 et juin 2026, la Suisse a importé 655 tonnes de myrtilles marocaines, pour une valeur supérieure à 7,6 millions d’euros. Ce volume constitue un nouveau record dans les échanges commerciaux entre les deux pays pour ce produit. La progression s’inscrit dans une dynamique installée depuis plusieurs années. Pour la troisième campagne consécutive, les exportations marocaines ont augmenté, leurs volumes ayant été multipliés par environ 2,3 en trois ans. Sur cette période, la croissance annuelle moyenne s’est établie à 33 %. Cette évolution a permis au Maroc de porter sa part à 5,5 % des importations suisses de myrtilles fraîches. Avec la hausse de 75 % enregistrée lors de la dernière campagne, le royaume a affiché la plus forte croissance parmi les pays fournisseurs mentionnés par EastFruit . Le marché reste toutefois dominé par l’Espagne, qui représente 44 % des importations suisses. Le Pérou arrive en deuxième position, avec 17,8 %, devant les Pays-Bas (7,8 %) et le Chili (6,4 %). Le Maroc complète désormais le groupe des cinq principaux fournisseurs. Un marché suisse en expansion Malgré sa taille relativement limitée, le marché suisse présente une valeur commerciale élevée et repose largement sur les importations pour satisfaire la demande en myrtilles. Celles-ci ont progressé pour la cinquième année consécutive, à un rythme annuel moyen de 10 %. Au cours de la campagne 2025-2026, les importations suisses ont atteint 11 800 tonnes, en hausse de 17 % sur un an. Cette progression témoigne de l’accroissement des approvisionnements nécessaires pour répondre aux besoins du marché. Les exportations marocaines s’étendent généralement de novembre à juin, avec un pic des expéditions au printemps, période qui correspond à une hausse saisonnière de la demande en Suisse. La progression du Maroc intervient dans un contexte contrasté selon les pays d’origine. Lors de la dernière campagne, les importations suisses en provenance de Pologne, d’Italie et d’Afrique du Sud ont diminué, tandis que les volumes en provenance d’Espagne, du Pérou, des Pays-Bas, du Chili et du Maroc ont augmenté. Parmi ces pays, le Maroc a enregistré la plus forte croissance. Cette percée permet au royaume de consolider sa présence sur un marché où les volumes importés continuent de croître et où la concurrence entre pays fournisseurs reste soutenue. items.title: NAFDAC uncovers another fake herbal factory in Lagos, arrests manager
items.description: By Chioma obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) on Thursday uncovered another illegal herbal products factory in Agege, Lagos, where three unregistered products were allegedly manufactured under unhygienic conditions, with one bearing a registration number belonging to a registered cough syrup. The agency sealed the facility, evacuated the products and arrested the manager, identified as Abulaziz Sayidu, for interrogation, while the alleged owner, Ashietu Adams, was said to have fled. The Deputy Director in charge of the Pharmaceutical Division, Investigation and Enforcement Directorate, NAFDAC, Pharm. Edith Joseph, who spoke during an inspection of the facility said the agency received intelligence on October 16 concerning the alleged production of Aishetu Adams Bitters with a fake NAFDAC registration number, prompting surveillance and intelligence gathering that led to the discovery of the facility concealed inside a residential building. “What we found was shocking. The facility was in a very poor and unhygienic condition. Look at the water they use for production and the environment where the manufacturing takes place. The products are manufactured outdoors, in the open air. I can tell you that this facility is not approved by NAFDAC,” she said. The products recovered were identified as Ashietu Adams Herbal Mixture for sexually transmitted diseases, Ashietu Adams Blood Purifier and another herbal preparation purportedly used for high blood pressure. Joseph said none of the three products was registered with NAFDAC, adding that the registration number displayed on the blood purifier belonged to a registered cough syrup. “The number belongs to another registered product, which is a cough syrup. They simply copied the number and placed it on their product to deceive Nigerians,” she said. According to her, the products were manufactured without regulatory approval, while their packaging lacked the manufacturer’s name and a verifiable address to establish their origin. She said the agency had sealed the facility pending further investigation and taken the recovered products to its office. Joseph disclosed that Sayidu claimed to have worked with Adams for about a year and assisted in managing the business, particularly when she travelled. The manager reportedly told officials that Adams, whom he identified as a Ghanaian woman, had travelled to Ghana. The agency said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the operation and the whereabouts of the alleged owner. NAFDAC WARNS CONSUMERS Joseph warned Nigerians against relying solely on NAFDAC registration numbers when purchasing herbal medicines and other regulated products, noting that counterfeiters could copy legitimate numbers to give unregistered products the appearance of regulatory approval. She advised consumers to verify product details through NAFDAC’s online verification platforms and the agency’s Greenbook. “If the name displayed does not match the product being presented, consumers should know that something is wrong,” she said. She urged consumers, particularly those in rural communities with limited internet access, to visit the nearest NAFDAC office for assistance in verifying the authenticity of products before purchase or consumption. The deputy director identified the absence of a valid registration number, manufacturer’s name and verifiable address as major warning signs, adding that the agency was intensifying surveillance and enforcement operations against illegal manufacturing outlets. Also speaking during the inspection, Deputy Director of Public Relations, NAFDAC, Mrs Christiana Obiazikwor, called for increased public participation in the fight against counterfeit and unregistered products. Obiazikwor warned landlords and property owners against allowing their premises to be used for illegal manufacturing activities, noting that those found to be aiding criminal operations could face prosecution. She urged property owners to monitor activities on their premises and report suspicious operations to the appropriate authorities. “We cannot fight this battle alone. Every Nigerian has a role to play in identifying and reporting places where illegal manufacturing activities are taking place,” she said. Obiazikwor said NAFDAC was expanding public awareness through radio programmes, multilingual jingles and community sensitisation campaigns, including its “NAFDAC and Your Health” programme. She said the agency also conducted awareness campaigns in local government areas, churches and schools to educate Nigerians on how to identify suspicious products and report illegal manufacturing activities. Emphasising the importance of product traceability, she said consumers should check details such as the manufacturer’s address and batch number rather than relying solely on a registration number. “These products do not have batch numbers or the manufacturer’s address. These are important details that help establish the identity and traceability of a product,” she said. She added that the agency was working towards stiffer penalties for offences involving the manufacture and distribution of counterfeit and unregistered products. NAFDAC urged members of the public to report suspected illegal manufacturing activities, assuring them that reports would be handled discreetly. The post NAFDAC uncovers another fake herbal factory in Lagos, arrests manager appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Minority demands independent parliamentary inquiry into Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse allegations
items.description: The Minority in Parliament is demanding an independent parliamentary inquiry into how earlier complaints of alleged sexual abuse against the suspended headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) were handled, including whether there was any political interference. The demand follows a JoyNews investigation by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, which reported allegations of sexual abuse involving as many as 19 female students at the school, including allegations of rape. Speaking to journalists in Parliament on Thursday, October 22, 2026, Deputy Minority Leader and Chair of the Minority Women’s Caucus, Patricia Appiagyei, called for justice for the alleged victims and accountability for officials found to have mishandled complaints. Ms Appiagyei outlined four demands, beginning with a thorough investigation into every allegation and prompt advice from the Attorney-General on the case docket already submitted. “We demand immediate action on one, a thorough investigation of every allegation; prompt advice from the Attorney-General on the submitted docket; and prosecution wherever the evidence warrants,” she said. She added that public updates must protect the complainants’ identities and preserve the integrity of the investigation. The Minority also called for immediate protection, counselling, medical care and legal assistance for affected students. Ms Appiagyei said any intimidation or retaliation against complainants must be investigated promptly. Its third demand is an independent inquiry into the handling of earlier complaints, including any possible political interference. The caucus wants the inquiry to identify officials responsible for any failures and recommend appropriate sanctions, while ensuring that students’ identities are protected in any published report. The fourth demand is for the responsible ministers to make a statement to Parliament detailing the chronology of events, actions taken and measures being implemented to protect students. Ms Appiagyei also called for confidential reporting channels within schools that operate independently of any head teacher accused of abuse. The allegations have drawn national attention following the JoyNews investigation, which detailed claims involving several students and raised questions about how earlier complaints were handled. Police have forwarded the case docket relating to one complaint to the Attorney-General’s Office for study and advice. Authorities have clarified that the docket concerns that individual complaint, while other allegations would require separate investigations. The headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, has been interdicted by the Ghana Education Service pending investigations. The NDC General Secretary, Fiifi Kwetey, has said the party will not shield Mr Abdulai and has called for an independent investigation by law enforcement authorities. Mr Abdulai has also served as the NDC constituency secretary for Juaben and had been seeking to contest the constituency chairmanship. He later withdrew from the race amid pressure within the party. The allegations against him have not been established in court. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The Minority’s demands add to calls for education authorities and other state institutions to ensure that complaints of abuse are properly investigated and that students have safe, confidential ways to report misconduct. The proposed inquiry would focus on the handling of earlier complaints, including whether officials failed to act appropriately or whether political considerations affected the response.

items.title: ICC Wins EU Parliament’s Sakharov Prize
items.description: Click to expand Image The International Criminal Court in The Hague, Netherlands, July 2025. © 2025 Nicolas Economou/NurPhoto via AP Photo (Brussels) – The European Parliament on October 22, 2026, awarded the Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and its officials. The following quote can be attributed to Philippe Dam, EU advocacy director at Human Rights Watch: “By awarding the Sakharov Prize to the ICC, the European Parliament recognizes the court’s vital role for victims of the gravest crimes around the world, at a time of unprecedented attack from the Trump administration and others. This prize should be a rallying cry for ICC members to stand up for the court and for the EU Commission to urgently activate the EU’s ‘blocking statute’ to protect the court and those supporting its work from effects of US sanctions.”

items.title: Des produits agricoles jetés dans la nature : la justice lance une enquête
items.description: La justice se penche sur le phénomène de la spéculation et vise particulièrement une pratique scandaleuse, celle qui consiste à jeter ou détruire des produits alimentaires, notamment la tomate, pour éviter la baisse des prix . Le parquet général près la Cour d’Alger a ordonné l’ouverture d 'enquêtes sur ces pratiques, indique un communiqué de la même juridiction diffusé ce jeudi 22 octobre. Des vidéos montrent des personnes en train de jeter des produits alimentaires Le procureur général a ordonné aux services de police judiciaire relevant des différents corps de sécurité, sous la supervision du Pôle national de lutte contre le crime organisé, d’ouvrir « des enquêtes immédiates, urgentes et exhaustives », à la suite de la diffusion de vidéos sur les réseaux sociaux montrant « des personnes à bord de camions en train de jeter des denrées alimentaires de grande consommation et des légumes de toutes sortes, propres à la consommation, dans des lieux situés en dehors du tissu urbain, dans le but d’empêcher leur distribution, de créer une pénurie sur le marché et de spéculer sur leurs prix », lit-on dans le communiqué. Identifier tout coupable, « quels que soient son statut ou sa fonction » Les enquêtes visent à identifier toute personne ayant participé à ces actes, ayant incité à les commettre, les ayant financés ou en ayant tiré profit, « quels que soient son statut ou sa fonction », précise-t-on. Elles visent aussi à débusquer « les réseaux et les ramifications qui se cachent derrière ces agissements, à retracer les circuits des marchandises ainsi que les réseaux de stockage et de distribution ». Les personnes impliquées seront déférées devant les autorités judiciaires compétentes afin qu’elles soient « poursuivies avec toute la rigueur prévue par la législation en vigueur », conclut la Cour d’Alger. Lors de la réunion du Conseil des ministres de dimanche dernier, le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a ordonné au Premier ministre, Sifi Ghrieb, d’ouvrir des enquêtes sur les pratiques frauduleuses et la spéculation qui entourent les opérations de commercialisation des viandes importées. items.title: Elmina Sharks FC goalkeeper William Donkoh undergoes leg amputation after motor accident
items.description: National Division One League Club Elmina Sharks FC have released an official statement announcing that their goalkeeper, William John Donkoh, has undergone a leg amputation following a motor accident. The Board and Management confirmed that the goalkeeper was involved in an incident in Cape Coast on Tuesday, October 20. Donkoh sustained severe injuries to his left leg and was rushed to the hospital, where he underwent emergency surgery on Wednesday, October 21. The club revealed that despite the medical team’s best efforts to salvage the limb, his left leg had to be amputated. Elmina Sharks expressed deep sorrow over the tragic event and reaffirmed their support for the player and his family during this challenging period. “The club will stand with William and his family throughout his recovery and beyond. William remains a valued member of the Sharks family”, the statement read. The club further called on the wider Ghanaian football community and well-wishers to keep Donkoh and his family in their prayers while appealing for privacy as he begins his rehabilitation process.

items.title: Conseil des Ministres du 22 octobre 2026 : 2 800 milliards FCFA pour « l’Énergie pour Tous » dans 10 ans et Création de la Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB)
items.description: Le Conseil des Ministres s'est réuni ce jeudi 22 octobre 2026, sous la présidence du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, Président du Faso, Chef de l'État, Président du Conseil des Ministres. Selon le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias TRAORÉ assurant l’Intérim du Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, le Conseil a délibéré sur les dossiers inscrits à son ordre du jour et pris des décisions importantes pour la bonne marche de la Nation, conformément aux orientations de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). Pour le compte de la Présidence du Faso, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création de l'Initiative Présidentielle Énergie pour Tous « Faso Wa-Fulu », en langue nationale san. Portée par le Ministère en charge de l'Énergie, cette initiative d'envergure nationale vise à garantir un accès généralisé à l'électricité d'ici à 2030. D’un coût de plus de 2 800 milliards FCFA sur 10 ans, le programme s'articule autour de 4 composantes que sont les Brigades d'électrification, l’Inclusion communautaire, l’Accès énergétique et la Souveraineté énergétique. « Cette initiative vise à accélérer l’accès de l'énergie pour tous à l'horizon 2030. C'est une initiative qui va s'étaler sur une période de 10 ans, avec une première période d'accélération de la prise en charge des questions énergétiques et une seconde phase de 5 ans qui sera consacrée à la consolidation des acquis », a expliqué le Ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, le Camarade Yacouba Zabré GOUBA. Naissance de la Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB) Au titre du Ministère de l'Industrie, du Commerce et de l'Artisanat, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création d’une société d'économie mixte à participation publique majoritaire dénommée Société viticole du Burkina Faso (SOVIB). Pour le Ministre du Commerce, de l'Industrie et de l'Artisanat, le Camarade Serge Gnaniodem PODA, cette société d'économie mixte est dotée d'un capital initial d’un milliard FCFA avec une participation de 45 % pour l’État, 10 % pour BRAFASO et 45 % pour le secteur privé burkinabè. « La SOVIB permettra la création de centaines d’emplois et la transformation de vignes produites au Burkina Faso », a soutenu le Ministre PODA. Cette unité industrielle sera basée à Bobo-Dioulasso, et nécessitera un investissement d'environ 9,8 milliards FCFA. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs1.60 per litre, raises high-speed diesel rate by Rs1.64
items.description: The government on Thursday decreased the price of petrol by Rs1.60 per litre, but raised that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.64. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs377.71 per litre while HSD will cost Rs391.75 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 23 (Friday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: TRANSLOG Africa 2026 : Des recommandations pour renforcer la souveraineté logistique africaine
items.description: Ouverte le 20 octobre 2026, la 5e édition du Symposium international sur le Transport et la Logistique en Afrique (TRANSLOG Africa) 2026 s’est refermée, ce 21 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. À l’issue des travaux, les participants ont formulé des recommandations visant à maîtriser la chaîne logistique afin de garantir et de renforcer la souveraineté africaine. Ces recommandations s’adressent aux États, aux organisations sous-régionales, aux autorités portuaires, au Conseil burkinabè des chargeurs (CBC) et aux centres de formation. En matière d’information et de digitalisation, le CBC est invité à concevoir et à diffuser la suite du portail de renseignements officiels du système national de gestion. Les participants souhaitent également que les États et les organisations sous-régionales renforcent l’interopérabilité des plateformes numériques ainsi que le partage sécurisé des données entre ports, douanes, escales des corridors et opérateurs privés. Les coûts logistiques ont aussi été examinés. Les autorités portuaires et le CBC sont appelés à analyser les coûts de stationnement dans la chaîne logistique, à identifier les dysfonctionnements et à adopter des mesures correctives appropriées. Les participants ont en outre insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer les compétences locales. Les centres de formation supérieure sont invités à développer une expertise nationale en ingénierie des projets d’infrastructures logistiques. Des recommandations pour renforcer la souveraineté logistique africaine -©Faso7 « Vos travaux ont posé un diagnostic lucide : vétusté des infrastructures, insuffisance de la digitalisation et de l’interconnexion des systèmes, guichet unique non opérationnel, persistance de pratiques anormales sur les axes et frais de détention qui alourdissent les coûts logistiques », a déclaré Émile Zerbo, ministre d’État chargé de l’Administration territoriale. Selon le ministre, l’objectif est d’améliorer la performance de la chaîne logistique, de simplifier les procédures et de renforcer la coopération régionale. Pour lui, il n'y a pas de souveraineté véritable sans une maîtrise de la chaîne logistique. Plateforme intergouvernementale Émile Zerbo a exprimé l’engagement du Burkina Faso à assurer le suivi de ces recommandations via un comité dédié et à encadrer juridiquement la reconnaissance de TRANSLOG Africa comme outil d’intégration africaine. « Ces recommandations ne sauraient demeurer lettre morte. Nous veillerons à la mise en place, dans les délais, du comité de suivi confié au Conseil burkinabè des chargeurs, et nous accompagnerons l’élaboration de l’instrument juridique consacrant la reconnaissance officielle de TRANSLOG Africa. (…) TRANSLOG Africa doit demeurer un instrument de coopération au service d’une Afrique qui décide par elle-même et pour elle-même », a-t-il déclaré. À noter que, lors de cette édition, le symposium TRANSLOG Africa a été institutionnalisé en tant que plateforme intergouvernementale et partenariale permanente dédiée à la concertation sur les transports, la logistique et la sécurité des corridors en Afrique. Elle a pour mission d’harmoniser les cadres réglementaires et juridiques du commerce et du transport transfrontalier. Cette plateforme permettra d’accélérer la digitalisation, la cybersécurité et la résilience des corridors logistiques. Elle facilitera également le dialogue public-privé et favorisera la mobilisation des investissements pour le développement et la sécurisation des corridors régionaux. Lazard KOLA Faso7 L’article TRANSLOG Africa 2026 : Des recommandations pour renforcer la souveraineté logistique africaine est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: À Béjaia, un CEM se dote d’un système d’alerte absence
items.description: Le CEM Abdelmoumen, à Béjaia, innove. Ce collège a installé un système électronique d’alerte pour surveiller l’absence des élèves. Les parents des élèves absents seront aussitôt informés par SMS. « Le système de suivi des absence des élèves du CEM a été mis en service. Il permet d’informer les parents de l’absence de leurs enfants 15 minutes après le début de la première séance », a annoncé l’administration de l’établissement scolaire, sur sa page Facebook. Béjaia : un CEM se dote dun système d'alerte absence, de quoi s'agit-il ? Ce nouveau système sera soumis à une période d’expérimentation d’une semaine pour évaluer sa performance », explique la direction du CEM Abdelmoumen, accompagné d’une vidéo montrant des élèves qui passent devant l’appareil d’enregistrement conçu pour scanner les cahiers de correspondance des élèves avec le procédé code-barres. L’introduction de ce nouveau système dans une école algérienne a suscité l’enthousiasme des internautes qui ont salué cette avancée. « Une bonne initiative. J’espère qu’elle sera généralisée dans toutes les écoles, », « une bonne chose ! A encourager », « une bonne initiative surtout s’ils vont ajouter des caméras de surveillance », lit-on dans les réactions. D’autres internautes n’ont pas manqué de faire quelques remarques : « Oui c’est une très bonne initiative ! Toutefois, cela devrait se faire avec une carte d’étudiant plutôt qu’avec un cahier de correspondance… ». D’autres commentaires ont évoqué l’aspect lié au problème de la surcharge dans la plupart des établissements scolaires. « Les derniers élèves vont arriver en retard dans les classe », « ce système convient seulement aux écoles ayant moins de 400 élèves », ont relevé des internautes. L’article À Béjaia, un CEM se dote d'un système d'alerte absence est apparu en premier sur TSA .
